articles.title: Sky Sports Scores App - frequently asked questions
articles.summary: Your questions about the Sky Sports Scores app answered, plus help and troubleshooting.
articles.body:
Not got the main Sky Sports app yet? It's even better than ever, with a new personalised video feed, free highlights and - if you're a Sky Sports subscriber - live streaming.

You can download it for free - just hit the buttons below if you're on your phone, or click the relevant link if you're on a laptop: iPhone & iPad | Android .

Do I need to be a Sky Sports customer to watch videos in the app?

Videos are accessible to all users. You don't need a Sky Sports subscription. Match action video clips require Sky iD.

Sky iD is a single username and password to access all of Sky's online services. Sky iD is freely available. You just need to register by providing an email address. You can access Sky iD from the app More menu.

Can I use the app when I'm not connected to the internet?

No. You must be connected to the internet to use this app and get live scores.

The app is updated as close to live as possible with live football scores, stats and other information.

Will the app work outside of the UK and Ireland?

You can access most of the app outside of the UK and Ireland. Some video content will not be viewable outside of the UK and Ireland. This includes English Premier League clips and English Football League action videos.

Depending on usage, the app can consume a large amount of data. If you are concerned about your data costs contact your network operator to ensure you have a mobile data bundle that meets your browsing requirements.

Why am I being asked to consent to storage and access of cookies, unique identifiers, personal data and information on my browsing behaviours?

To learn more about why we ask for this and what your privacy options are, please see our Sky Privacy and Cookies Notice.

You can amend your privacy options at any time from the More menu.

Initially, please check your internet connection. The scores will only update on a stable internet connection.

Try refreshing the screen by dragging the screen downwards and releasing. A loading icon will indicate the content on the screen is being updated.

If neither of the above options resolve the issue, try deleting the app, reinstalling it from the app or play store.

If you are still having issues, please contact support at apps@sky.uk with the subject 'Sky Scores Android App'/'Sky Scores iOS App' and an explanation of your problem and we will endeavour to help.

You can receive push notifications for your favourite team, followed teams and any games for which you tap the star icon next to the fixture.

To turn on notifications go to the more menu > notification preferences. On iOS you will be prompted to allow notifications by switching them on within your phone settings before you will be able to alter them within the app. Tap the button on the alert to be taken directly to the relevant phone setting.

I want to change my notification settings

You can turn on and personalise your notifications during onboarding when you first install the app.

You can change your notification settings at any time, including turning individual notifications on or off by going to the more menu > notification preferences. On iOS you will be prompted to allow notifications by switching them on within your phone settings before you will be able to alter them within the app. Tap the button on the alert to be taken directly to the relevant phone setting.

The schedules/line-ups/results look wrong

The Sky Sports Scores app updates information every 30 seconds. If information in the app appears to be incorrect please check you have a stable internet connection, as the app requires this to update data.

If neither of the above options resolve the issue, try deleting the app and reinstalling it from the app or play store.

Please check you have a stable internet connection as the app requires a live connection. Some videos require you to create a free SkyiD login in order to watch them. These videos will send you to an account creation/log in screen when tapped.

Some videos are only available in the UK, due to content distribution rights. If you are outside of the UK, the videos will not play.

If none of the above options resolve the issue, try deleting the app, reinstalling it from the app or play store.

You can follow a match by selecting the star symbol next to a Match within the Scores section of the app. You will receive notifications for starred games. Your notifications are managed within the notifications section of the More menu.

You can follow a new team from the app More menu. Select My Followed Teams and search for teams you want to follow by tapping the team crest or using the search bar. You can change your followed team at any time. Content will be personalised based on your selection.

You can change your favourite team from the app More menu. Select My Favourite Team and search for your favourite by tapping the team crest or using the search bar. You can change your favourite team at any time. The fixtures for your favourite teams will be pinned to the My Scores section.

You can change the competitions you follow from the app More menu. Select My Followed Competitions and search for your favourites by tapping the competition crest or using the search bar. You can select and unselect new competitions at any time. Some competitions may not become available to select until closer to their start date. Content will be personalised based on your selection.

You can toggle Sky Bet odds on or off from the app More menu.

If you're having issues with your SkyiD, please contact SkyiD customer support on 03442 411 522 (UK) or 0818 719 819 (ROI)

This could be a result of a poor internet connection. Please ensure you are connected to WiFi or a strong 3G/4G connection for the optimum experience.

I'm having another problem with the app. What should I do?

You are welcome to contact us if you encounter any problems with the app. Please email us at apps@sky.uk with the subject 'Sky Scores Android App'/'Sky Scores iOS App' and an explanation of your problem and we will endeavour to help.

articles.title: Anthony Gordon: England and Barcelona winger shrugs off consistency concerns to become key figure for club and country
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon has 10 goal involvements in his last 10 games for England, having shaken off questions about his consistency stemming from a poor final season at Newcastle; Gordon has become an integral part of Thomas Tuchel's line-up only months after place on left wing was not assured
articles.body:
It took until the final pre-World Cup warm-up with Costa Rica, where Gordon scored one and set up another, to finally nail down his spot for the tournament opener with Croatia. Even then, many of the Sky Sports writers were yet to be fully won over.

But barely three months on, he has become an integral name on Thomas Tuchel's team-sheet and one of his most valued attacking players.

Since a slow start to that World Cup, something has clicked. Blanks in England's first two games against Croatia and Ghana saw him dropped for the must-win final group match with Panama, but on his return he set up both of Harry Kane's goals in the comeback win over DR Congo.

Another assist against Norway plus a crowning goal in England's biggest game, the semi-final with Argentina, have brought the country and, perhaps, Gordon himself along too.

The Barcelona winger is now on a four-game international scoring streak - the longest of any player in the current set-up and of anyone not called Harry Kane in almost six years.

That would be an impressive run for any player, not least one whose attacking output was so openly questioned right up until the eve that summer tournament.

Gordon had struggled to recreate his best moments for his club in an England shirt until this year's showpiece, but now has 10 goal involvements in his last 10 games for his country as part of the most in-form front four in international football.

His reputation was been helped by a diffcult final year at Newcastle under the Premier League microscope, where he managed just five non-penalty goal involvements in the top flight. It understandably framed judgement over his ability - but only two seasons earlier he had produced four times that figure in his first campaign on Tyneside.

It frustrated him sufficiently to tell ITV ahead of this camp his "quality and football IQ" had not been respected by fans in England before moving to Barcelona.

Certainly, the talent has always been there. His first two years at Newcastle, and bits of his time at Everton, show it. But consistency, rather than talent, has long been the biggest concern for Gordon's coaches.

There was enough belief in Barcelona that they could get Gordon back to his best even before the World Cup that sporting director Deco and head coach Hansi Flick followed Tuchel's lead and looked beyond his Premier League struggles to sign him ahead of Marcus Rashford. That came despite paying more than double what his England team-mate would have cost.

It went under the radar more widely that only Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe netted more than his 10 goals in 12 games in last season's Champions League, including against his future employees in the League Phase. It had not gone unnoticed at the Nou Camp.

Perhaps it is ironic that in Gordon's recent interview he complained he was only valued for his work-rate and speed before moving to Barcelona, days after Deco told RAC1 in Spain it had been the winger's "intensity' which had attracted them to him in the first place.

But the 25-year-old has undoubtedly taken his game to the next level and proven himself in ways he had not before over these last few months on the domestic and international stage.

Prior to that Costa Rica showing he had produced only two goals and an assist in his first 18 England games.

With what we have seen since, there is no question he can step up in the biggest games. When England have needed answers, he has delivered, both in a World Cup semi-final as well as his strikes in the Nations League against Spain and the Czech Republic which were both match-changing interventions.

Gordon has always had the self-belief. That was clear the moment he revealed at his Barca unveiling he felt he would play for the club since the age of three, and had clearly been preparing long enough to deliver his speech in assured Spanish.

That World Cup run can have only built his confidence further, plus the tag of becoming the first Englishman signed permanently by Barcelona since Gary Lineker, 40 years ago.

He has hit the ground running at the Nou Camp, with fans' interactions already going viral on social media as they immediately warm to a player who has managed four assists in his first six LaLiga matches - double the number he laid on across his final season in the Premier League and the joint-most in the division this season.

Deco has made a point of publicly encouraging Gordon to improve his finishing, but his goalscoring run for England suggests that too will follow in time.

Whether he can keep up his bright start in Catalonia or his goalscoring form for England, or if long-term consistency remains his greatest struggle, will only be found out in the fullness of time.

But if he can, both club and country will have a serious player on their hands.

articles.title: Croatia vs Spain: UEFA Nations League – Yamal, Modric, head-to-head
articles.summary: Coming on the back of a 10-match winning streak, Spain face Croatia with sights set on the Nations League quarterfinals.
articles.body:
Who : Croatia vs Spain What : UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , Group A3 match Where : Stadion Poljud, Split, Croatia When : Tuesday, October 6, at 8:45pm local time (18:45 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT.

FIFA World Cup holders Spain can confirm their ticket to the UEFA Nations League quarterfinals when they face Croatia on their trip to Split.

With a perfect record in the tournament and an overall 41-match unbeaten streak, the odds swing heavily in Spain’s favour to clinch victory.

La Roja’s attack has been on fire this term – they have netted 10 goals from seven scorers in three games, with teenage sensation Lamine Yamal leading the scoring charts.

Unlike Spain, Croatia’s performance has been far from exemplary, with Luka Modric’s side suffering their heaviest defeat in history in the last fixture.

Before the clash of generations 2.0 between Yamal and Modric, Al Jazeera breaks down everything you need to know:

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against equally ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure, which features promotion and relegation.

The teams compete across four divisions, facing every other team in their group twice: Once at home and once away. The league phase ends in November.

In the top league, League A, the top two teams from each group advance to the quarterfinals, which take place in March 2027.

The finals will again be contested between four teams. The host and dates of the finals have not been confirmed yet.

How have Croatia and Spain played in the Nations League?

Croatia are third in this group with three points from three games.

Spain are first in the group with nine points.

Luka Modric and Ivan Perisic (Croatia): The evergreen Modric, very much the heartbeat of the Croatian midfield even at 41 years old, has found the net once in this campaign. His fellow experienced teammate, Perisic, has also been impactful with his two assists.

Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena (Spain): With four goals in three games, Yamal is the joint leading scorer in this year’s Nations League, alongside three others, including England’s Harry Kane. The Barcelona star has found the net in each game, including a double against Croatia in the initial face-off in Seville. Atletico Madrid’s Baena, on the other hand, has been influential in more ways than one, bagging two assists and a goal.

Centre-back Martin Erlic is sidelined with injury until mid-October, while Josip Juranovic is unavailable due to illness.

Probable Croatia XI : Dominik Livakovic; Josip Stanisic, Luka Vuskovic, Josko Gvardiol, Ivan Perisic; Luka Modric; Franjo Ivanovic, Petar Sucic, Mateo Kovacic, Martin Baturina; Petar Musa

As many as four Spain squad players are doubtful due to injuries: Ferran Torres (physical discomfort), Alejandro Grimaldo (thigh), Joan Garcia (knee) and Nico Williams (thigh).

Probable Spain XI : David Raya; Ivan Fresneda, Robin Le Normand, Aymeric Laporte, Fran Garcia; Rodri, Pedri; Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Alex Baena; Roberto Fernandez

articles.title: "Bellingham es aterrador, no había visto nada igual"
articles.standfirst: Alex Scott destaca que Jude Bellingham "es el mejor centrocampista del mundo, sin duda uno de los mejores jugadores del planeta"
articles.summary: Alex Scott destaca que Jude Bellingham "es el mejor centrocampista del mundo, sin duda uno de los mejores jugadores del planeta"
articles.body: Alex Scott, jugador del Bournemouth y de la selección inglesa, confiesa haber quedado fascinado por el "impresionante" nivel mostrado por Jude Bellingham con Inglaterra en la Nations League. El jugador del Real Madrid marcó un gol y repartió tres asistencias en la goleada por 0-7 ante Croacia. "Sinceramente, nunca había visto nada igual. Es aún mejor en persona; verlo de cerca y compartir el campo con él... Es el mejor centrocampista del mundo, sin duda uno de los mejores jugadores del planeta y, además, una gran persona", declaró Scott, que fue titular por primera vez con Inglaterra, sobre Bellingham. El futbolista del Bournemouth subrayó que "todo el mundo lo sabe: los aficionados lo saben y todo el mundo conoce su calidad humana". "En el campo el talento de Bellingham es aterrador y marca el nivel al que debemos aspirar, apuntó. Alex Scott (23 años) reconoció sobre Bellingham que "tengo su misma edad, pero para mí es un referente para los jóvenes futbolistas ingleses". Bukayo Saka, jugador del Arsenal, refrendó la opinión de Alex Scott sobre Bellingham (que ya ha sido 59 veces internacional con Inglaterra). "Jude Bellingham es sencillamente increíble. Se merecía el premio al Jugador del Año de Inglaterra". Roy Keane, leyenda del Manchester United, declaró en 'ITV' que "Bellingham puede llegar a convertirse en uno de los mejores jugadores de todos los tiempos". "Su actitud con la selección inglesa últimamente... lo he elogiado por ser fantástico con el balón, pero lo que hace sin él es lo que motiva a todos estos jugadores. Si tienes en tu equipo a un jugador tan bueno, que es increíble con el balón y juega en el Real Madrid y hace cosas brillantes, pero sobre todo su entrega sin balón, eso inspirará a todos los demás jugadores", explicó el exfutbolista.

articles.title: South Korea captain Lee Gi-hyuk apologises for gloating over military service exemption
articles.summary: Lee Gi-hyuk apologises for gloating about avoiding South Korea's mandatory military service.
articles.body:
South Korea captain Lee Gi-hyuk has apologised for gloating about avoiding mandatory military service after winning gold at the Asian Games.

His side beat hosts Japan 1-0 in the final and, afterwards, Lee held up his gold medal and triumphantly announced he was "not going to the military".

In a social media post reported by local media, , external the 26-year-old later said he was "deeply sorry to the fans who are currently fulfilling their military duty, as well as to all those who sincerely supported us".

South Korean males are, in most circumstances, required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of active military service before the age of 28.

However, the government rewards Asian Games champions and Olympic medal winners of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.

Golfer Tom Kim also avoided military service by winning gold at the Asian Games.

Athletes who have previously secured the exemption include former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who served for only three weeks in 2020 having won the Asian Games with his country two years earlier.

"As an adult I should have thought carefully before speaking," added Lee, who was one of the overage players in his country's Under-23 squad and plays for Gangwon FC in South Korea's K League.

"I deeply regret having spoken so carelessly, and I will continue to reflect on my actions.

"I sincerely apologise to all the fans who have supported us wholeheartedly and who are doing their utmost to fulfil their military duty."

articles.title: Raúl Varela responde a Mbappé tras su mensaje a La Tribu: “Su comportamiento es impropio de una estrella del Real Madrid”
articles.standfirst: El director de La Tribu analiza la reacción del francés después de que Javier Tintó desvelase su malestar por el escaso apoyo en la carrera por el Balón de Oro
articles.summary: El director de La Tribu analiza la reacción del francés después de que Javier Tintó desvelase su malestar por el escaso apoyo en la carrera por el Balón de Oro
articles.body: La reacción de Kylian Mbappé en redes sociales a una información contada en La Tribu ha tenido respuesta de Raúl Varela. El francés ironizó haciendo referencia a su tía abuela después de que Javier Tintó explicase en Radio MARCA el supuesto malestar del delantero por el apoyo recibido en su carrera por el Balón de Oro. “Ayer nos acostamos en la bella y acogedora Split, costa adriática de Croacia donde juega España, sabiendo una cosa más. Kylian Mbappé tiene tía abuela”, arrancó Varela con ironía antes de detenerse en la repercusión de lo contado en el programa. “También aprendimos otra cosa importante: que al igual que ocurría con Ancelotti camino del entrenamiento en Valdebebas, la gente del aspirante a Balón de Oro también está muy pendiente cada mañana de La Tribu y de lo que se diga en este programa”, señaló. Varela recordó el origen de la información, desvelada por Javier Tintó: “El caso es que un tribuno bien informado, Javier Tintó, harto de las lesiones de Mbappé de 15 días y sus posteriores viajes a recuperarse no se sabe dónde, en esta ocasión parece que entre Madrid, Francia y Suiza con bicicleta de por medio, le dio por preguntar”. Según relató el director de La Tribu, la respuesta obtenida por Tintó apuntaba directamente a la carrera por el Balón de Oro: “La respuesta que obtuvo y compartió en La Tribu fue que Mbappé anda mosca con el escaso, por no decir nulo, apoyo que el Madrid por un lado y la selección francesa por el otro le han dispensado en esa carrera por el Balón de Oro que también ansía Lamine y Kane y alguno más”. Mbappé reaccionó posteriormente en redes sociales y Varela recogió el guante: “Mbappé ironizó en redes sociales contestando a La Tribu, cosa que agradecemos, porque sus más de 136 millones de followers solo en Instagram repartidos por el mundo se enteraron de que existimos”. Varela continuó con la referencia utilizada por el propio delantero: “Hizo alusión a su querida tía abuela, a quien no tenemos el gusto de conocer y a la que le deseamos una larga y próspera vida junto a su sobrino nieto”. El periodista también señaló que Mbappé “ya ha regresado, por fin, a la Ciudad Deportiva de su club, aparcando la bicicleta y apurando su recuperación para ver si puede estar disponible el sábado ante el Villarreal”. Fue entonces cuando lanzó su crítica más contundente al francés: “Un gesto que le acerca al público de a pie, ese que no entiende nada de lo que pasa, ni con sus ‘chorrocientos’ goles que no sirven para ganar títulos ni con ese comportamiento tan suyo y tan impropio de una estrella del Real Madrid”. Varela cerró su opinión recurriendo de nuevo a la ironía y mencionando a varios futbolistas con pasado madridista: “Quizá si le preguntase a la tía abuela, qué sé yo, de Carvajal, Nacho o Lucas Vázquez, le podría explicar algo necesario, pero ese es otro problema, que en este Real Madrid tampoco hay tías abuelas que sepan lo que le hace falta al club”.

articles.title: Croacia - España: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el partido de la Nations League
articles.standfirst: Los detalles del encuentro de la Nations League
articles.summary: Los detalles del encuentro de la Nations League
articles.body: La selección española de fútbol afronta en Split un compromiso decisivo en su andadura por la UEFA Nations League. El conjunto dirigido por Luis de la Fuente se presenta a la cita instalado en un pletórico estado de forma, avalado por una racha histórica de encuentros sin conocer la derrota y con el objetivo prioritario de certificar matemáticamente su clasificación para los cuartos de final del torneo. Pese a contar con ausencias destacadas por lesión y motivos personales en la expedición, la campeona del mundo buscará imponer su identidad de juego basada en la posesión y en la capacidad de desequilibrio de piezas como Lamine Yamal y Dani Olmo para firmar un pleno de victorias. Por su parte, la selección de Croacia llega al duelo envuelta en un ambiente de alta tensión y necesidad tras encajar un doloroso 0-7 frente a Inglaterra en su última comparecencia. El cuadro balcánico, sacudido por las duras críticas recibidas tras esa histórica derrota, tratará de apelar a su tradicional orgullo competitivo para lavar su imagen ante su público en el Estadio Poljud. Con la presencia en el esquema de veteranos ilustres como Luka Modric e Ivan Perisic, el equipo local buscará cerrar espacios, contener las acometidas españolas y aprovechar sus opciones a balón parado para frenar la dinámica triunfal del bando rival. El partido entre Croacia y España, correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la UEFA Nations League, se disputará este martes 6 de octubre a partir de las 20:45 horas (horario peninsular español). El encuentro entre la selección balcánica y el combinado español se podrá seguir en directo y en abierto por televisión en España a través de La 1 de TVE, así como por la plataforma RTVE Play. Sigue toda la actualidad de la selección española, el minuto a minuto del partido y la mejor cobertura del Croacia - España en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

SEVILLA, 29/09/2026.- El centrocampista de la selección croata Luka Modric, durante el partido de la segunda jornada de la Liga de Naciones que España y Croacia disputan este martes en el estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, en Sevilla. EFE/Julio Muñoz

articles.title: Inglaterra - República Checa: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el partido de Nations League
articles.standfirst: Los detalles del encuentro de la Nations League
articles.summary: Los detalles del encuentro de la Nations League
articles.body: La selección de Inglaterra afronta este nuevo compromiso de la UEFA Nations League pletórica tras firmar una histórica exhibición goleadora frente a Croacia (0-7). Bajo las órdenes de Thomas Tuchel, los 'Three Lions' desplegaron una versión arrolladora liderada por un brillante Jude Bellingham y la voracidad anotadora de Harry Kane, demostrando una abrumadora superioridad colectiva. Instalados en una dinámica altamente positiva y con el firme objetivo de pelearle la primera plaza del grupo a España, el combinado británico buscará aprovechar el aliento de Wembley para imponer un ritmo vertiginoso desde el pitido inicial y sumar tres nuevos puntos. Por su parte, la República Checa llega a la cita necesitada de sensaciones positivas tras encajar una trabajada derrota por 3-1 ante España en Oviedo. El conjunto dirigido por Santi Denia plantó batalla e hizo dudar por momentos al combinado español en la segunda mitad, pero la falta de contundencia en las áreas terminó por condenarle al traspié. Frente a un escenario de máxima exigencia como el feudo inglés, la plantilla checa necesitará cuajar un ejercicio defensivo prácticamente perfecto, minimizar las pérdidas en la fase de creación y explotar el balón parado para intentar dar la sorpresa de la jornada. articles.title: 'Not here to be tourists in Argentina': Benin goalkeeper ahead of Lionel Messi's farewell match
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Benin goalkeeper Marcel Dandjinou has made it clear that Argentina’s farewell celebration for Lionel Messi will not stop his team from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Benin goalkeeper Marcel Dandjinou has made it clear that Argentina’s farewell celebration for Lionel Messi will not stop his team from competing. As Benin prepare to face Argentina at the Monumental, the 28-year-old goalkeeper says his focus will be on doing his job, even if that means denying Messi a goal on his final night.Dandjinou, who plays for Kruger United in South Africa’s Premier Division, spoke to Spanish newspaper Marca after arriving in Buenos Aires.Despite reports of problems with Benin’s preparations, including claims about poor hotel facilities and difficulties in training, he insisted the team had been treated well."We did not face any problems. We are fine here in Buenos Aires. Why do you say that? The truth is that we have had good conditions," he said.‘We are here to compete’Dandjinou admitted that facing Messi makes the match particularly special, but stressed that Benin are not travelling to Argentina simply to watch the superstar."For me, this match is not like any other match. I think it is an opportunity that will not come again, because it is Messi's last match. It is a special match. But, look, we are here for Argentina and for Messi, but we must not forget that we represent our country too," he added."We are here to defend Benin. This is football: eleven players against eleven. We can win, or draw, or they can win, but it is football. We are not here to be tourists in Argentina; we are here to play and to compete. It will be a great day in our lives."The goalkeeper has huge respect for Messi, having grown up watching him play."For me, Messi is one of football's legends. We grew up watching him play. He is one of our favourite players. To be able to play against him now, on the same pitch, is incredible. I never imagined this would happen, but it will happen on Tuesday. For me, Leo is a legend, a true legend," he further remarked.No free goal for MessiAsked whether he would allow Messi to score a penalty in the final minutes as a farewell gesture, Dandjinou gave a firm answer."No, no. I am a goalkeeper, and my job is to save the ball. Even if it is the final minute and a penalty is awarded, if Messi takes it, I will try to save it. It is that simple: it is football. Yes, we are here to celebrate Messi, but no one has asked us to give him a goal. And knowing Messi, there is no need to give him anything. If he wants to score, he has to do his best to achieve it," he explained.While every Benin player would love Messi’s shirt, Dandjinou joked that the squad could need plenty of them."If you asked any player in my team, he would tell you he wants his shirt. So it would be great if they made a lot of shirts and gave one to each player. Because if only one of us goes to ask for the shirt, I do not think it will be easy: we all want one," he continued."It would be a great honour for me to play, and that memory will remain engraved in my mind forever. During my career I will be able to say: I was there, in the last match of a legend, in Messi's last match. It is incredible."On the eternal Messi-Cristiano Ronaldo debate, he concluded, "We grew up watching Messi and Cristiano. They taught us a lot about football. They have been competing for a long time. articles.summary: El astro rosarino juega esta próxima madrugada (01.00 en España) su último partido con la Albiceleste
articles.body: Leo Messi se despide esta próxima madrugada de la Selección argentina (01.00 horas en España, Movistar). Un día tan histórico como triste para un país que ve cómo uno de sus símbolos históricos no vestirá más la Albiceleste. Será una noche llena de sorpresas ante un rival atípico, Benín, continuando los rivales africanos que se iniciaron con Burkina Faso (7-0) del sábado. “Si hubiera habido cinco Monumentales, se hubiera llenado”, dijo Scaloni en rueda de prensa. “Me escribieron de todos lados. Creo que está todo dicho, sólo quería disfrutarlo. Me imagino a todo el mundo emocionado, incluido él. Desde que pise el Monumental será un día inolvidable para todos. Agradezco ser parte de su día”. Será la despedida al jugador más determinante en la historia del país, en base a los títulos logrados en su último lustro con la Selección: dos Copas América (2021 y 2024), el Mundial 2022, y la anterior Finalissima, más otras dos finales mundialistas, ambas perdidas (2014 y 2026, ante La Roja). En total, 207 partidos(se quedará en 208 con el de esta noche) y 125 goles totales para un ‘extraterrestre’ de este deporte que hoy llenará el estadio Mas Monumental con todos los honores (ha habido tortas por conseguir una entrada). El astro rosarino llegó el domingo a Buenos Aires y ya se entrenó con el equipo para preparar la fiesta que le prepara la AFA y el público argentino. “Tenemos todavía dos entrenamientos con él y sólo nos queda disfrutar del poco tiempo que queda”, confesaba Scaloni. “Bienvenido, Capi de mi vida”, expresó Chiqui Tapia al recibir a Leo en Ezeiza antes de sumarse a la concentración. Habrá muchas sorpresas y lo único seguro es que el ‘10’ jugará de inicio. ¿Cuánto? No han trascendido los detalles, pero sí está asegurada la presencia de todos los campeones de 2022 y de los subcampeones de 2026. La única ausencia de renombre será la de Ángel di María —tiene compromiso con Rosario CentraL— con quien ha compartido gran parte de su trayectoria en la Albiceleste. Juntos comenzaron su andadura ganando los Juegos Olímpicos de 2008... y llevaron a Argentina a lo más alto cuando parecía que el destino tenía otros planes preparados. La leyenda de Leo es inconmensurable. Se va con todos los registros posibles de la Albiceleste. Ni siquiera Diego Maradona, en números, le hace sombra: más finales disputadas (11); más títulos en la absoluta (4); más años en la Selección (21); más partidos (207); más victorias (134); más partidos como capitán (147); máximo goleador (125); seis Mundiales; tres finales; récord absoluto de partidos (34) y goles (21) en la historia mundialista... y más y más. “Su legado es las ganas de querer estar siempre. Era el primero en llegar y el último en irse. Cómo se cuida, cómo afronta cada partido. Son cosas que no se ven pero sus compañeros sí y es el mejor ejemplo que puede haber. Deja algo inigualable”, explicaba Scaloni. “Es muy raro que aparezca un jugador así. Por lo que hace en el campo y lo que transmite fuera. Disfrutemos de esto”.

articles.standfirst: Hasta 10 jugadores han marcado en este inicio de temporada: la pasada campaña sólo 13 futbolistas vieron puerta
articles.summary: Hasta 10 jugadores han marcado en este inicio de temporada: la pasada campaña sólo 13 futbolistas vieron puerta
articles.body: El equipo más realizador de LaLiga Hypermotion es el equipo que más goleadores suma a la causa. El gol en el Eibar es cosa de todos. El líder de Segunda se está destapando en su versión más realizadora con 18 dianas en 8 jornadas. Ha marcado en todos sus partidos, promedia más de dos goles en cada uno de ellos y hasta 10 jugadores han visto puerta en estos dos primeros meses de competición, una muestra clara de que el Eibar no depende de la inspiración de sus delanteros para marcar. De hecho, Bautista y Martón sólo han marcado un gol cada uno y la mediapunta es la que está saliendo al rescate con su aportación goleadora. Guruzeta, con tres dianas, encabeza la lista realizadora del Eibar, seguido de Adu Ares, Magunazelaia, Iván Gil, Álvaro Rodríguez y Mada, todos ellos con dos tantos. Aleix Garrido, Pejiño, Bautista y Martón completan la nómina anotadora de los armeros. Casi la mitad de la plantilla ya sabe lo que es marcar en estas ocho jornadas. La pasada temporada sólo 13 jugadores fueron capaces de ver puerta y esta temporada está cerca de igualar esa cifra en apenas dos meses de competición. A excepción de Elijah Gift y Eric Pérez, que no superan los 30 minutos de participación, los demás jugadores de ataque han estrenado su casillero goleador esta temporada. Pejiño ha sido el último jugador en sumarse a la lista de goleadores. De entre las cualidades de Jokin Aranbarri siempre ha destacado la de ser un gran gestor de grupo. El sábado, en Albacete, con 1-2 en el marcador y el rival apretando, decidió dar entrada al andaluz, sin demasiado protagonismo en este inicio de competición, pese a que el contexto demandaba otros cambios. Sin embargo, la apuesta le salió redonda, porque Pejiño hizo el tanto de la sentencia y salió reforzado del Belmonte.

articles.title: Larrubia: "Somos los mismos que subimos y lo vamos a conseguir"
articles.standfirst: El ’10’ del Málaga se sienta con MARCA para analizar el inicio de LaLiga y los problemas que está teniendo el equipo para conseguir la primera victoria
articles.summary: El ’10’ del Málaga se sienta con MARCA para analizar el inicio de LaLiga y los problemas que está teniendo el equipo para conseguir la primera victoria
articles.body: David Larrubia es el alma y uno de los mejores representantes del Málaga de Primera. El ’10’ malagueño se sienta con MARCA para analizar el comienzo de LaLiga y los problemas que está teniendo el equipo para conseguir la primera victoria. Canterano malaguista desde los 10 años, Larru confía en que este bloque de jugadores va a conseguir la permanencia y defiende a capa y espada el estilo de juego que propone Funes. “Somos los mismos y lo vamos a conseguir”, dice. Pregunta. ¿Cómo están llevando estas semanas algo raras, sin partidos? Respuesta. Bien. Al final no estamos acostumbrados a estos parones de selecciones, pero creo que nos está viniendo bien. Nos está metiendo mucha caña el míster. El otro día tuvimos dos días libres, que también creo que nos han venido bastante bien. Cuando estás en una racha en la que no ganas y todo te sale cruz, parar un poco, no pensar demasiado las cosas y darle tranquilidad a lo que estamos haciendo, creo que nos va a venir bien. P. ¿A qué le están dando más caña en este periodo sin partidos: al aspecto físico o al mental? R. Un poco al tema físico y, sobre todo, a volver a lo que fuimos el año pasado: generar muchas ocasiones, tirar muchas puertas y llegar al área con gente. Estamos haciendo mucho hincapié en eso, sobre todo con la gente de arriba, porque no estamos del todo finos en estos primeros siete partidos. P. ¿Por qué cree que el Málaga no se ha adaptado y no ha conseguido resultados? R. No lo sé, pero la realidad es que hay equipos como Villarreal, Real Madrid o Atlético en los que, en los últimos 30 minutos, se nota que son equipos grandes de Champions que te pasan por encima. Se les da la mano y se les aplaude porque han sido mejores que tú. Pero creo que en muchos partidos, sobre todo contra Levante y Deportivo, hicimos un buen partido y tuvimos méritos para ganar, pero no se dio. P. Se está poniendo mucho el foco en la falta de gol… R. Creo que es un poco global, pero es verdad que, viendo cómo fuimos el año pasado, este año no estamos haciendo las mismas entradas al área ni estamos siendo tan determinantes ahí. Creo que llevamos bien la pelota hasta tres cuartos de campo y ahí se nos está apagando la luz. Es una realidad y en eso tenemos que centrarnos para mejorar. P. ¿Está notando personalmente el cambio de categoría? R. Lo estoy notando, pero sobre todo en los futbolistas de nivel. Yo, por ejemplo, contra equipos como Levante o Deportivo no he notado gran diferencia. Pero cuando te enfrentas al Madrid, ves a Bellingham o Mbappé y sabes lo que van a hacer, pero da igual porque lo hacen. Sabes que va a ir hacia la derecha y se te va porque tiene otro punto de velocidad. Creo que nosotros vamos a conseguir ese punto de velocidad y de chispa de la categoría, pero necesita un proceso. P. Es importante que no entren esos nervios, que no aparezca la presión o la ansiedad… R. Al final, cuando estás mucho tiempo sin ganar, esas cosas aparecen en el público y en los medios de comunicación. Frustra un poco porque tú ves que lo das todo, que el equipo lo da todo en cada partido y que en los entrenamientos cada jugador se deja el alma. Después no sale el resultado y frustra, porque ves a la gente enfadada. P. El Málaga corre… R. Por correr, este equipo no va a dejar de correr. Es verdad que tenemos que mejorar. Yo recuerdo ver los datos de Vinicius después del partido contra el Madrid y mi sensación era que no corría en el partido, que iba andando. Te pones a ver sus datos físicos y duplica a todo el mundo en alta intensidad. Y te quedas pensando: 'Si no se ha movido de su esquina durante el partido...'. Al final te sorprende, pero son jugadores que están a otro ritmo, a otra velocidad. Tenemos que intentar igualarlo o estar cerca de ellos. P. El partido del Getafe es de los que duelen… R. Sí, nos jodió mucho porque creo que mejoramos muchas cosas del partido anterior. Llegamos al área, tuvimos una ocasión dudosa que no nos dieron, estuvimos bien con el balón y ellos creo que en la primera parte no nos hicieron mucho peligro. En la segunda es verdad que desajustamos un poco la presión, nos salieron con cierta facilidad y, a partir de ahí, empezaron a sacar centros, que es donde son más peligrosos, y empezamos a sufrir. Es verdad que, después de la primera parte que hicimos, duele perder los tres puntos. P. ¿Cómo ven el siguiente partido contra el Espanyol? R. Lo tenemos con muchas ganas. Sabemos que tenemos dos partidos en casa y queremos hacer los máximos puntos posibles. Queremos empezar a hacer de La Rosaleda un fortín, que la gente se contagie de la energía positiva y, a partir de ahí, sacar los máximos puntos posibles. P. Mucha gente piensa que cuando el Málaga consiga esa primera victoria va a ser otra cosa. R. Yo creo que sí. Al final, muchos jugadores tenemos que sacar nuestra mejor versión. Sabemos que es complicado tener el estado de forma que, por ejemplo, yo tuve el año pasado durante los últimos tres meses, igual que Chupete. Es complicado mantenerla durante todo el año. Recuerdo que el año pasado, hasta la jornada 12, no metí mi primer gol y sentía esa presión de querer hacerlo al principio. Y mira cómo acabó la temporada. ¿Quién me lo iba a decir? Que después de marcar contra el Andorra y ponerme a llorar, iba a meter el gol del ascenso. P. ¿Qué os llega del entorno? R. Yo, por suerte, noto que la gente me tiene mucho cariño por la calle y no me dice nada malo. Me dicen que hay que seguir, que jugamos bien. Algunos dicen que ya hay que ganar, pero te sueltan la típica. Creo que la afición está contenta con el equipo. P. ¿Os ha sorprendido que Funes haya mantenido la misma idea de juego? R. Hay que mantenerla porque sabe los futbolistas que tiene, las cualidades que tienen y la manera de jugar idónea para el equipo. Creo que es la que él inculcó cuando llegó. No hay que cambiar, hay que cambiar a lo mejor matices y mejorar el plano físico, pero nuestra manera de jugar es bonita y ha dado resultados. Hay que seguir con eso. P. Ignacio Camacho dice que tenéis que seleccionar mejor esos partidos en los que sois tan alegres R. Es cierto. Al final somos una plantilla muy joven y pecamos a veces de novatos en la categoría. A veces por querer dar un pase de más, hacer un control bonito o lo que sea. Tenemos esos roles de jugadores con poca experiencia, pero creo que conforme vayan pasando las jornadas nos adaptaremos mejor y sabremos jugar mejor con los minutos. P. Soñando con ese primer gol en Primera... R. Todos los que no hemos marcado todavía tenemos ganas de meter nuestro primer gol en Primera, pero ahora lo importante es que el equipo empiece a ganar. Me gustaría que fuese en casa o contra el Sevilla o el Betis... P. ¿Cómo ve al míster? ¿Cómo está de ánimo? R. Bien. Creo que el míster es una persona que sabe cuándo hablar, lo que habla y el momento en el que lo dice. Es una persona que tiene una transparencia total y mantiene mucho la tranquilidad y el seguir haciendo lo que nos ha hecho fuertes. Eso nos da mucha tranquilidad. El míster nos dice que, igual que nosotros, él también es un novato en la categoría. Él no se esperaba estar aquí y también tiene que aprender muchas cosas y mejorar muchas cosas. P. ¿Qué tal los fichajes? R. Por mala suerte, algunos han estado mucho tiempo lesionados, pero bueno, esta semana recuperamos a Calero, que creo que nos va a aportar muchísimo. Aznou ha empezado a entrenar esta semana y vemos que es un chico con mucha calidad. Y después Cajuste, que espero que la semana que viene empiece a entrenar ya. Es un tío con físico, que no tenemos mucho. P. ¿Y experiencia? Es quizás lo que falta un poco en la plantilla… R. Sí. Sabemos que somos una de las plantillas más jóvenes de LaLiga, pero tenemos a Calero, a Einar, a Barros... Son jugadores que nos están aportando esa veteranía. Nos dicen que esto es muy largo y que tenemos que estar tranquilos. Y yo creo que los fichajes, sobre todo como personas, Loren siempre acierta. El que viene aquí no desarma el equipo y va a la par de todos. P. La gente quería más fichajes… R. Entiendo, pero estamos los de la casa. Que esos jugadores decidan quedarse y apostar por el club que ha ascendido creo que es por algo más que dinero o fichajes. Sentimos que nos debemos al Málaga, que nos lo ha dado todo, y teníamos esa ilusión por jugar con el Málaga en Primera. Al final, cuando los jugadores se van, la gente los valora. Y cuando los tienen, valoran lo que tienen los demás, los fichajes. P. No hubo opciones de irse… R. Claro. A lo mejor ofertas como tal no. Pero al final, al que más y al que menos, a la puertecilla le han tocado. Yo, en mi caso, nada más terminar el partido de Almería, por la emoción, ya le dije a mi representante: 'El año que viene estoy aquí, pase lo que pase'. Yo no he recibido nada. P. Un mensaje para el malaguismo. R. Que somos los mismos que ascendimos el año pasado. Muchos me han dicho que ese es el problema, que somos los mismos y que no nos hemos reforzado. Yo estoy convencidísimo de que, de la misma manera que hemos ascendido de Primera RFEF a Primera, vamos a sacar adelante lo de este año.

articles.body: La primera plantilla del Betis ha regresado este martes a los entrenamientos para seguir preparando su próximo compromiso liguero, el domingo en La Cartuja frente a Osasuna, en la intensa serie de partidos que tiene por delante tras la fecha FIFA de selecciones. Y lo ha hecho, precisamente, recuperando ya a algunos de los futbolistas que se fueron durante el parón con sus respectivos combinados nacionales. Troy Parrott, convertido en uno de los máximos artilleros de la Nations League, ha vuelto al grupo tras su periplo con Irlanda. Abde, quien también vio puerta con Marruecos estos días, se ha sumado igualmente al grupo. Mismo caso que el canterano Morante, goleador con la sub 20 y que está ya a las órdenes de Pellegrini, disponible para enfrentarse al conjunto rojillo el fin de semana en el duelo correspondiente a la octava jornada de la competición doméstica. El que también se ha incorporado de nuevo al trabajo con sus compañeros ha sido Marc Bartra. El central catalán fue sustituido en los primeros minutos del último partido de su equipo, en Riazor frente al Deportivo de la Coruña, y durante las dos últimas semanas, tras descartarse que sufriera una lesión, ha llevado a cabo un plan personalizado de entrenamientos. Hoy es ya uno más y tampoco debe tener problemas para jugar ante Osasuna. Ruibal ha vuelto a comenzar los rondos con el equipo, aunque sigue con su proceso de recuperación. De este modo, las ausencias han sido las del lesionado Junior, que espera parte médico del problema que sufrió con su selección, y las de los internacionales Fran García, Facundo Bernal, Manu González, Ángel Ortiz, Álvaro Fidalgo, Giovani Lo Celso y Valentín Gómez que siguen con sus selecciones. Los canteranos Rodrigo Marina y Borja Alonso han completado el grupo.

articles.title: El parón liguero llenó la enfermería del Celta
articles.standfirst: Cuatro lesionados en estas dos semanas
articles.summary: Cuatro lesionados en estas dos semanas
articles.body: El Celta confiaba en aprovechar la ventana de selecciones para recuperar a diferentes futbolistas y sin embargo ha sucedido todo lo contrario, elevando el número de integrantes de su enfermería. Hasta cuatro jugadores se han lesionado o han sufrido problemas fiscos en estas dos últimas semanas, dos de ellos estarán de baja el próximo mes y medio: Miguel Román y Carl Starfelt. Miguel Román se lesionó en Vigo y fue operado de la rodilla derecha. Estará de baja entre mes y mes medio. Mientras, Starfelt se lesionó con su selección y estará también un mes y medio de baja por una rotura fibrilar con afectación en el tendón del muslo derecho. Dos bajas sensibles que se perderán como mínimo los nueve próximos encuentros de los célticos. Otros dos futbolistas se han lesionado estos días con sus selecciones. Radu sufrió molestias en el hombro, que no le deberían impedir jugar el domingo en Elche, y Sebastián Cáceres que con molestias de pubis es duda para esta jornada. A ellos hay que sumarles a Jones El-Abdellaoui, que fue operado de la rodilla izquierda días antes del parón y al que le quedan semanas de recuperación, y también Iago Aspas, que pronto espera estar de vuelta tras la rotura fibrilar sufrida hace poco más de tres semanas.

articles.title: Inside Monaco’s academy with Eric Dier: How this ‘unique’ football club is back at the top of the Ligue 1 table in France
articles.summary: Monaco are top of the table in Ligue 1 and the secret of their success runs deeper than the summer appointment of Filipe Luis. Sky Sports goes inside their famed academy in order to speak to players and staff, including Eric Dier, to find out how they keep doing it…
articles.body:
"I like that kind of detail," Eric Dier tells Sky Sports . "It is very special." Dier is a senior figure at Monaco now but it resonates with him from his time as a youngster at Sporting. "It makes you feel you are in the right place to make that journey as well," he adds.

"Because of how they have been successful that gives a lot of confidence to the young guys to be in an academy where so much talent comes through. They see a clear pathway. They know they are at a club that knows how to do it. It is a remarkable place."

For Monaco's general manager Thiago Scuro, creating that feeling among the current crop of academy talent has never been more important. Monaco are without Champions League money this season and the race for young players is heating up too.

If Monaco are to find a way forward in the modern game, it means leveraging La Diagonale like never before. But with quality players continuing to emerge and the club top of the table in France under new coach Filipe Luis, there is real optimism again.

"Imagine how inspiring it is for a 15-year-old kid coming to live in La Diagonale," Scuro tells Sky Sports . "There are a lot of factors that Monaco a very special place for young players and a big part of our strategy is investing in the academy to help develop them."

Dier describes Monaco as "unique" while Scuro points out that this is effectively a country playing club football. "We have a mission to represent the Principality." But there are practical reasons too why Monaco is ideally positioned to bring through talent.

Necessity is the mother of invention and this is a club whose success is built on the academy. "We need to be able to develop players to be able to compete at the top level because we do not have a big stadium. We only have 36,000 people living in Monaco."

Modest crowds can mean more time for players to grow. "The level of pressure inside the club suits young players," explains Scuro. "They can take chances, make mistakes and go again." Even so, Henry and Mbappe were both French title winners at Monaco.

But Henry was gone by 21, Mbappe by 18. That alone indicates the trend towards top talents moving on more quickly these days. It is putting far greater pressure on clubs like Monaco not just to keep hold of young players but to recruit them in the first place.

"The competition for young, talented players has gone to another level," concedes Scuro. "Ten years ago, clubs like Monaco, Benfica, Porto, Ajax and Lyon would recruit young players and develop them." The food chain was always there but it took time.

"If they succeeded then they would reach the Premier League, they would reach Madrid or Barcelona. But the reality is that in the last decade, more and more of those clubs are going directly to recruit 17 and 18-year-olds. This has forced us to adapt our strategy."

Monaco are going younger now. "We are more and more focused on early-stage recruitment." Paris-born Mamadou Coulibaly came to the club aged just 15. "At the start, it was hard because not everyone has to leave their parents," he tells Sky Sports .

"I had to adapt. I worked a lot on my mentality, to become a man. I just say thanks to the educators during my time with the academy. I progressed with them a lot and made friends. At Monaco, yes, it is a beautiful place. But the football side of it is also top."

Coulibaly is 22 now, a starter, along with Dier, in the recent 2-1 win away to Paris Saint-Germain. That he is into his fourth season with the first team owes a little to injury. Others, such as Aladji Bamba, have come and gone for big money in the meantime.

Scuro is not sure it is ideal. Monaco can be an important step in the journey. He talks of football pushing "too many players from this path" and how it is "starting to have an impact on how good these boys can become" if they skip this development phase.

With the emphasis on even younger players, it only increases the importance of players like Dier. "This is where we try to create the balance," says Scuro. They aim to have around one-third of the squad made up of older players who can set the standards.

"Young players also need reference inside the dressing room. They need experienced players to give sustainability to the team but also to guide those players daily on how to behave, how to learn, how to work. They became a strong source of inspiration."

As well as Dier, there is captain Denis Zakaria. Aleksandr Golovin is now into his ninth season at the club, while Lukas Hradecky adds experience in goal. Dier takes the responsibility seriously. He has even taken on a coaching role at the academy.

"I really enjoy it. The club, academy director Manu Dos Santos, the coach of the under-17s, they have been so welcoming and open to me. It has been a fantastic experience to spend time with them and try to develop myself and try to help them at the same time.

"To spend time with the young boys at the start of their journey, it is great to be a part of that and to help them if I can, even in the smallest way. For me, I feel a bit of a sense of responsibility. I feel like football deserves it from me for what it has given to me."

Dier's main responsibility remains as a defender for the first team and that is going particularly well right now. Monaco have won four and drawn one of their first five games, having also negotiated the play-off round of the UEFA Conference League.

New head coach Filipe Luis, the former Chelsea and Atletico Madrid left-back, has made a big impact. "It is always a pleasure for a player when you work with a coach where you feel you are learning new things and being pushed to improve," says Dier.

"I love working with him. I think you can see a really consistent, gradual improvement in the team, moving towards what he wants and what we are working on every day. I think you can really see a clear style and clear principles of play in every phase of the game."

Scuro was impressed with Filipe Luis' work at Flamengo, where he won the Copa Libertadores last year. "We know how hard it is to do what he did." Importantly, he developed individuals too. "Changing the behaviour of the players at Flamengo."

He adds: "He can help us to give another step in our football project, which is becoming a better team, especially in possession." The signs are promising even if the deadline-day drama that saw Folarin Balogun and Lamine Camara stay brings ongoing issues.

The finances remain challenging as a result. "Last season, we were not able to deliver the same level of success and this creates a big impact on the way that we manage the team," says Scuro. "It is very important to consistently play in the Champions League."

But as ever with Monaco, the salvation can be found not just on the first-team pitch with Filipe Luis but at La Diagonale. "Our main goals is to be a top-three club in France systematically through players development and a very clear playing style," he adds.

"Developing players is crucial for us." And so it goes on for Monaco. A trio of teenagers in Safouane Benzahra, Oumar Kounate and Anis Soubeir all made their professional debuts in August with Benzahra going on to make his Ligue 1 bow in the win over PSG.

"It is incredible. Every time a kid comes to train with us it is always impressive," says Dier. "Players are produced all over the country now," adds Scuro. "But the reality is that Monaco has a much longer history of this." That next bedroom is waiting to be named.

articles.title: Marc White exclusive: Dorking Wanderers chief on new co-owners, EFL dreams and ambitions of becoming 'the world's local club'
articles.summary: Dorking Wanderers owner and manager Marc White tells Sky Sports what new investment from Frank Villares, Debra Tucker and James Sixsmith changes, the club's huge social media audience and why he believes reaching the EFL would be "one of the world's greatest sporting successes"
articles.body:
It is more than likely you will have seen one of his rants go viral on social media. In that respect, he is one of a kind.

But he also has no equal in the way that he set up Dorking Wanderers with a group of friends in 1999 - and is still there, 27 years on. The chairman, the manager, the face of the club.

After a recent FA Cup second qualifying round win over Southall FC, he posted from the club's X account: "Thanks for tonight to all of our loyal supporters & never forget we were in Crawley & District Division 5. Step 17."

It has been a long, long journey. One that has cost millions and taken in an incredible 12 promotions.

Dorking finished 16th in the National League in 2022/23 - their best ever finish and the closest they have come to the EFL, which is the stated goal. At this point, why would it not be?

Currently, they are back in the National League South - but now White has significant additional backing.

US entrepreneur Frank Villares had first become involved in Dorking in 2024, through the 'Rise With Us' campaign, which allowed the public to buy shares in the club to help them achieve their goals. A £180,013 target was set, with £333,180 the actual figure raised by 746 investors.

In the summer, he and his wife Debra Tucker were announced as co-owners and growth investors.

"Frank and Debra are massive English football fans and there's this huge enthusiasm for the English pyramid in the US as that's the one thing the US money can't buy," says White, speaking to Sky Sports in a room overlooking the club's Meadowbank home.

"They were actually looking around for a bigger interest in a club. They wanted to be more involved and I was actually helping them with that, telling them what to watch out for.

"They'd gone to four or five clubs and a deal fell through last minute so I just said: 'Don't forget, there's always Dorking Wanderers!' It just felt like everything had gone wrong for a positive reason. Then they were like, 'You know what, we've already said to ourselves we love Dorking, why are we even doing this?!'

"They are both 40 plus VAT and they're in a position now in life where they want to really enjoy and have a project and they want to win - Frank has even put a picture of the team at Wembley, an AI job, on his vision board!

"They're perfect because they trust us to run it, but they want to be involved as well. This is just the beginning."

In addition to Villares and Tucker, a consortium led by former professional ice hockey player James Sixsmith acquired a shareholding in the summer.

"We want to surround this club with people that want to succeed and want to win and James is very similar," adds White.

"We're really lucky. James and Daryl [Cumberland] from his consortium are part of that mechanism behind it all. As we go up the divisions and as we find more success, their involvement will become greater and greater.

"I want to say to the people involved: 'Listen, here's the thing. If we put in another X million, we could actually get to the Championship or we can build a stadium and we can do X, Y and Z. We've got big players in our setup that are going to enable us, not just financially, but also in terms of decision-making and having the right mindset towards growth.

"The legacy of Dorking Wanderers is to find a way to progress. What people love about the club is the underdog story of coming from nowhere to somewhere. We have to find a way for that to continue."

"The investment has made things easier. But in football, everything you do, whether it's on or off the field, costs a lot of money. We're by no means set for life, not in a million years. We're just in a position where we can add some things, largely off the field.

"But that kind of off-field investment can generate more income, which we can invest on the field, hopefully. That's where the success cycle comes; win more games, more fans, promotion, more fans.

"There's not one football club in the world that really profits. You might get the odd one but, in general, someone somewhere is putting time, effort and money into a football club. Off the field is the largest part of the football club.

"You're in the entertainment business and you've only got one show a week normally. The rest is all hard work."

Speaking of, White is, naturally, one of the central figures on the YouTube channel Bunch of Amateurs , which documents all the behind-the-scenes goings-on at Dorking.

The channel currently has more than 200,000 subscribers and a global audience.

"We had half a billion unique views last year of the club. Half a billion. Ten times the average Premier League club. My thing is to part capitalise on that, but part deliver. Imagine what happens to that with more promotions?

"As a result, every single match there's someone from Australia, New Zealand or America. They'd be the three top places every game.

"I went down to Costa one morning to get a coffee. It opened at 7am and I looked like I'd just been f*****g dug up. Two people came in with these Dorking Wanderers shirts on. They were American and had just got off a flight and they couldn't believe they'd seen me.

"It's a bit surreal like that, but it's all positive. I like the recognition I get. I don't really get any bad words about me from anyone that knows the game. I quite like the recognition of the hard work that's gone into it because it would be easy just to think I just swear at refs. Obviously, there's a lot more to me!"

Throughout the interview, White keeps coming back to V2 - the next version of the club.

"V1 took us from the park fields to where we are today," he says. "Everything is teeing up this club to have a V2. We're better equipped now.

"I think we need to get promoted again really soon. Next year or two minimum. We then need to try and do a bit of a double and then try and break into the Football League.

"I think breaking into the Football League genuinely will make us one of the world's greatest sporting successes. As big as that sounds. I don't know f*****g any others!"

One potential obstacle is that, while White has been so successful at Dorking, he does not hold the coaching badges necessary to manage in the EFL.

"We'll take care of that, that's fine," he says. "The dream really is to be in there. I'd love it."

But the ambitions extend far beyond the EFL.

"I feel like we really want to be the whole world's local club," White says.

"We believe we're the pioneers of like real, relatable content with a local football team. It's given us this global stage and that trying to capitalise on that and people feeling like they belong to a local community, even if they live in Mississippi.

"Frank tells me he can't believe how many times he gets stopped in America - even in Texas, someone said to him 'I love Dorking!'.

"We want to just like continue to put the club on a global reach - and we identify with the fact that winning will be a part of that. So we have to find a way to win."

As for this season, Dorking are currently eighth in the National League South, three points behind leaders Maidstone United. A trip to Dover Athletic - a point and a place above them - beckons on Saturday.

"Standard stuff, really. Stressful. We've done alright. Loads of injuries, all that s**t. Standard modern football," says White as he picks up his bag, ready to dart to a podcast record.

"Dorking are always in the mix, so we'll be there again."

There is no time for sentimentality - only the next challenge.

articles.title: Scanning offers players like Martin Odegaard an edge as football becomes faster and more intense
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Nick Wright tried out virtual reality technology designed to train scanning to see how some players are improving their off-the-ball awareness; Martin Odegaard, Aurelien Tchouameni, Marc Guehi and Romeo Lavia are among those to have used it
articles.body:
After a short countdown, a passage of build-up play begins at the feet of a virtual team-mate. My task is to receive the ball and choose the appropriate pass, all while every movement of my head, and every subsequent decision, is logged and analysed.

The technology, created by Be Your Best , is designed to train scanning, those little glances from side to side made by players to gather information about their surroundings which can be used to inform their decisions when they receive the ball.

Mercifully, my first attempt is at 80 per cent speed, allowing me to find my bearings. I start slowly as I am tackled while dwelling on the ball but feel smugly satisfied as I am praised for a 'critical scan' before finding a team-mate with a pass through the lines.

When the dial is turned up to 100 per cent, replicating the speed of a top-level game, I am given a reality check. I think better of trying the 120 per cent setting incorporated after a request from Martin Odegaard when he used the headset for the first time.

The Arsenal captain, renowned for his vision and speed of thought, is the type of player who fascinated Andreas Olsen, CEO of Be Your Best , when Olsen was an academy player at Viking FK in Norway.

"It was mind-blowing to me how some players just seemed like they had eyes in the backs of their heads," he tells Sky Sports .

"When it came to that skill, I felt like I didn't have the vocabulary to understand or describe what it was. I just remember wishing I was as good as them at understanding where the opponent's pressure was coming from and where the next pass should go."

It was around the same time, in the late 1990s and early 2000s, that Norwegian professor Geir Jordet began studying what would come to be known as scanning.

His research, focused on the period of 10 seconds before a player receives the ball, found that high scan rates were a defining feature of the world's best players.

"Those 10 seconds are critical," says Olsen. "It's all about making a decision before you get the ball. When you've already made that decision, you're not going to be surprised by what happens. All the pictures have been taken, so it's just about executing."

Barcelona and Spain legend Xavi Hernandez stood out as the most prolific scanner in Jordet's research. "He wasn't the fastest player on the pitch in his legs, but in his mind he was the fastest player, so he didn't need to be super quick," says Olsen.

"He made his decisions before he got the ball, and then the ball was gone. Or he turned left because he knew the pressure was coming from the right. Watch clips and you see it. He always covers the ball with his back because he knows where his opponent is."

Scanning is not a new concept. Frank Lampard recalls it being drilled into him as a boy by his father, who shouted the word "pictures" from the sidelines. But its importance is growing as the game becomes quicker and time available on the ball is squeezed.

Premier League tracking data shows players are sprinting much further per game, on average, than even a few years ago, continuing an upward trend as pressing proliferates and intensity increases.

"Arsene Wenger said we've solved all the physical aspects of football," says Olsen. "We know how to get faster and we know how to get stronger. We are really clear about that.

"But in a world where football is becoming way more physical, we also have to pay attention to how fast the mind works. It's not enough to be the strongest and fastest on the pitch anymore."

That applies to defenders as well as attackers. Dan Micciche, a former England and Arsenal youth coach working in Saudi Arabia's national team set-up, describes watching a defensive scanning masterclass from Giorgio Chiellini and Leonardo Bonucci.

"I was at Wembley, behind the goal where Italy were defending in the first half of the Euros semi-final against Spain in 2021," he tells Sky Sports . "Literally, all they did in the first half is what I would describe as skipping and scanning. They never really sprinted, even up the pitch or to the side, they were just jogging.

"Normally, we tell a centre-back or a defender to know where their man is. But it was as if those two knew where every player on the pitch was, and it gave them a sense of calm."

Most agree nowadays with the premise that situational awareness and scanning can be trained. But some are sceptical about the specific benefits of doing so using virtual reality.

"I always think the game is the best teacher, and the observation and feedback of a coach looking at the details," says Micciche. "You can improve players by asking good, open questions. What did you see? Why didn't you turn? Where was the space?

"It sounds very simple but it's not simple to do because, in our sport, we want everything instantly. We maybe rush to telling them, either in action, so they don't need to scan because we've made the decision for them, or by giving them the answer when we ask them because we don't have the patience for a longer dialogue.

"It's about spending time with a player and having a lens on individual actions. Also, I've seen players who just scan to please the coach. Are they actually observing their next move, or are they just thinking about how many times they move their heads?"

It is an issue Be Your Best have attempted to address in the development of their technology by measuring the timing of a player's scans while wearing the headset as well as the frequency, and by grading the quality of their decisions.

The company point to examples they say demonstrate the benefits. In a nine-week programme involving Germany U16 and U17 players , Olsen says scan rates improved by 28 per cent, while coaches reported better positioning in 80 per cent of the players.

They cite individual success stories too. Manchester City centre-back Marc Guehi is a user of the technology. Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia has even invested in the company.

And, most notably, in 2023, Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni used the technology to familiarise himself with the centre-back position when told he would be drafted into the role during an injury crisis.

After helping the side keep a clean sheet in a 4-0 win over Osasuna, the midfielder posted about using the headset on social media.

Using it myself, it is easy to understand the appeal. I leave knowing my scanning still needs considerable work. Odegaard's 120 per cent setting will have to wait for another day. But I find myself intuitively checking my shoulders as I walk towards the station.

articles.title: UEFA to investigate spitting incident at Ireland-Israel football match
articles.summary: An Israeli player is accused of spitting on an Irish coach as the teams returned to their dressing rooms at half-time.
articles.body:
European football’s governing body says it will open a disciplinary investigation into an incident involving an Israeli player, who is accused of spitting on a member of Ireland’s coaching staff during the second leg of their politically charged Nations League fixture on Sunday.

The probe will look into “any potential misconducts from player(s)” during the match played in Serbia, UEFA told Al Jazeera in an emailed statement on Tuesday.

“Following a review of the official reports which contained an allegation of an incident in or around the tunnel at half-time, an UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspector has been appointed to conduct the appropriate disciplinary investigation regarding potential misconducts from player(s),” said the full statement.

Tempers flared and words were exchanged on and off the pitch at the TSC Arena in Backa Topola on Sunday.

Following the match, Irish media reported that Ireland’s athletic coach Damien Doyle had accused an Israeli player of spitting at him after the half-time whistle.

Asked about the spitting incident at the post-match news conference, Ireland’s head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson declined to provide details.

“I was there. I’m not going to comment. It’s something a disciplinary committee will look at,” he said.

Hallgrimsson admitted there had been a number of incidents that could have escalated during the game.

“We were clever enough to stop it before it went too far,” he told Ireland’s public broadcaster RTE after the match.

“I felt that was the intention [from Israel], to intimidate us and make us do something stupid. I give big credit to the players and how they handled their emotions.”

Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had left the sideline at the time of the incident and did not see what happened.

“Half-time, I was in the dressing room, in my room with my ⁠⁠⁠⁠staff; I didn’t see anything. When I’m going to see and check, I will get ⁠⁠⁠⁠back to you with the answer,” he told reporters.

articles.title: José Ballester, Hijo Predilecto de Valencia
articles.standfirst: El fundador y primer presidente del Levante fue galardonado con esta distinción
articles.summary: El fundador y primer presidente del Levante fue galardonado con esta distinción
articles.body: osé Ballester Gozalvo, fundador y primer presidente del Levante UD, es desde el día de ayer Hijo Predilecto de la ciudad de Valencia. El consistorio de la capital del Túria otorgó este galardón al padre del conjunto granota en las distinciones, que se entregan anualmente en fechas cercanas a la festividad del Nou d'Octubre, día de la Comunitat Valenciana. El actual máximo mandatario de la entidad, Pablo Sánchez, fue el encargado de recoger, en manos de la alcaldesa, María José Catalá, dicha distinción en nombre de la familia en el consistorio de la ciudad. “Su legado trasciende a su familia y termina perteneciendo también a la memoria colectiva de una ciudad. Nació en el Cabanyal, fue maestro, pedagogo, abogado, periodista, político y pionero y arquitecto del fútbol valenciano, pero quizá la mejor manera de definirlo sea como un hombre profundamente comprometido con València y con la idea de que una sociedad mejor se construye desde la educación, la cultura y la participación democrática”, apuntó la alcaldesa de la ciudad. La concesión de la distinción de Hijo Predilecto supone la culminación de un proceso de justicia histórica iniciado y respaldado por el Levante UD. En abril de 2024, el club impulsó las gestiones para cumplir la última voluntad de José Ballester Gozalvo y su esposa, Teresa Molins Gausach: regresar a su tierra natal. Tras la exhumación de sus restos en Francia y un sentido homenaje en la Llotja VIP L'Alqueria del Estadi Ciutat de València, el matrimonio fue sepultado en el cementerio del Cabanyal, el barrio costero que vio nacer a nuestro fundador. Un acto que homenajeó a otros deportistas valencianos Junto al reconocimiento a José Ballester Gozalvo, el Salón de Plenos municipal distinguió a otras figuras del deporte valenciano como a la atleta Fátima Diame; mientras que el titulo de Hijos Adoptivos recayó en los futbolistas Alex Grimaldo y Ferrán torres, entre otros.

articles.title: Konaté completa todo el entrenamiento y apunta al Villarreal
articles.standfirst: El francés participa con normalidad en la sesión del martes, con Fede aún en el gimnasio
articles.summary: El francés participa con normalidad en la sesión del martes, con Fede aún en el gimnasio
articles.body: El Real Madrid sigue preparando el duelo del sábado ante el Villarreal. En la sesión de este martes, Ibrahima Konaté estuvo sobre el césped de Valdebebas, participando con normalidad en el entrenamiento, que completó sin problemas. El internacional francés tiene por tanto opciones de estar disponible el regreso de los blancos a la Liga, después de tener que abandonar la concentración de Francia a causa de un problema muscular. Además de Konaté, también Militao participó en la sesión de trabajo de los blancos en Valdebebas. En brasileño sigue quemando etapas en su proceso de recuperación, y hay opciones de que entre en la lista de convocados para el duelo ante el Submarino. Sobre todo, para volver a entrar en la dinámica del grupo e ir recuperando sensaciones colectivas. El que no aparece en las imágenes facilitadas por el club Fede Valverde, que no viajó con Uruguay durante esta pausa internacioanl a causa del esguince de tobillo sufrido en el derbi tras una entrada de Kang-in Lee que no fue sancionada por el árbitro del partido ni revisada por el VAR. El uruguayo trabajó en el gimnasio, a la espera de su evolución en los próximos días de cara a una posible participación en el partido del regreso a la Liga del Madrid. De momento, no está ni mucho menos descartado.
