articles.title: Acuerdo cerrado entre Carvajal y el Getafe a falta del OK de LaLiga
articles.standfirst: El ex jugador del Madrid se convertirá en jugador azulón si hay luz verde en el control económico
articles.summary: El ex jugador del Madrid se convertirá en jugador azulón si hay luz verde en el control económico
articles.body: El Getafe está muy cerca de hacerse con el fichaje de Dani Carvajal, sin equipo desde que el pasado 30 de junio finalizara su contrato con el Real Madrid. La noticia, adelantada por Abc, ha despertado la ilusión de la afición azulona y cuenta con el respaldo de José Bordalás, principal valedor de una operación que permitiría incorporar experiencia, calidad y carácter al equipo. El lateral ha pasado el verano entrenándose en solitario, a la espera de una propuesta que le convenciera para iniciar una nueva etapa en su carrera. Tras cerrar su trayectoria en el conjunto blanco, Carvajal ha optado por tomarse un tiempo antes de decidir su futuro. En los últimos días ha aparecido la posibilidad del Getafe, con el que no han tardado mucho tiempo en ponerse de acuerdo. La operación todavía debe cristalizar y tiene al control económico de LaLiga como mayor dificultad, ya que el salario de Carvajal en el Real Madrid era muy elevado y el límite del club azulón era mínimo. Y aunque Carvajal en ningún paso percibiría lo que ganaba en el Madrid, la operación debe tener la luz verde de LaLiga. Es el último paso que le falta al fichaje. Para Bordalás, su llegada supondría un refuerzo de peso tanto en el campo como en el vestuario. Su experiencia, su competitividad y su capacidad de liderazgo son argumentos que explicarían el interés del técnico, que nunca ha dejado de mirar al mercado para reforzar una plantilla corta.

articles.title: La montaña rusa de Antonio Casas
articles.standfirst: El delantero cordobés tendrá que frenar por lesión tras su primer doblete en el Sporting
articles.summary: El delantero cordobés tendrá que frenar por lesión tras su primer doblete en el Sporting
articles.body: Antonio Casas no desaprovechó la oportunidad ante el Celta Fortuna. El delantero cordobés fue el elegido por Nicolás Larcamón para sustituir al lesionado Juan Otero y liderar la delantera rojiblanca en la visita del filial vigués a El Molinón. No defraudó el 17 del Sporting, que vivió una montaña rusa de emociones en su primer día en solitario al frente del ataque gijonés. Doblete, sustitución y alerta a la vista en cuestión de minutos. La remontada del Sporting no se entendería sin Antonio Casas. El andaluz puso la primera piedra para darle la vuelta al marcador con un gol de olfato. Aprovechó el error defensivo de Anxo Rodríguez, se adelantó al guardameta Coke Carrillo y remató a placer para poner el empate. Al filo del descanso, Casas repetiría tras forzar la expulsión de un jugador visitante. Golazo de falta directa y celebración a lo Cristiano Ronaldo para encaminar al Sporting hacia la victoria y convertirse en el nuevo pichichi rojiblanco. No tendría tiempo para más. Tras el descanso, el Sporting regresó al césped con la llamativa ausencia de Antonio Casas, que había sufrido unas molestias musculares en la primera parte. El ex del Córdoba apunta a sufrir una pequeña rotura de fibras en los isquiotibiales que le obligará a frenar durante las próximas semanas. Una parada obligada tras su explosión goleadora en el Sporting de Gijón. Otro golpe más para Nicolás Larcamón. La de Antonio Casas es la última lesión de la plaga sufrida por el Sporting en las últimas semanas. Un problema que ya se trata en la Escuela de Fútbol de Mareo. "Es urgente. Haremos una reunión ahora mismo, no me quiero ir de este estadio sin atender mejor a qué estamos fallando", confesaba el entrenador argentino su preocupación por el alto número de lesiones. Una lista a la que se sumó Antonio Casas tras su primera gran tarde como jugador del Sporting de Gijón.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 5
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith is poised to leave Ohio State with a jam-packed trophy case. He's making a serious run at adding a Heisman Trophy to that collection.
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith is poised to leave Ohio State with a jam-packed trophy case. He's making a serious run at adding a Heisman Trophy to that collection.

Yes, two full months remain in the 2026 college football season. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is keeping pace. Alabama QB Keelon Russell is steadily bolstering his own résumé. The race is not close to finished.

But right now, we have an undisputed leader in Smith.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss (+1500)

Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State (+3500)

Nate Sheppard, RB, Duke : As the Blue Devils have notched a 4-0 start, Sheppard has totaled 714 scrimmage yards and nine touchdowns. Duke, which has only ACC games remaining, plays at Georgia Tech in Week 6.

Josh Hoover, QB, Indiana : The transfer from TCU remains unblemished this season after throwing for 251 yards and four touchdowns in a 47-15 rout of Rutgers. Hoover has tossed 15 scores and committed zero turnovers for 5-0 Indiana, which travels to unbeaten Nebraska this Saturday.

Austin Simmons, QB, Missouri : Simmons is also an interception-less standout. He's passed for 1,287 yards and 13 touchdowns, most recently putting up 340 yards and two scores in a shocking 45-17 upset of Florida. Mizzou, now 4-1, is set to host Texas A&M.

Arch Manning, QB, Texas : Following an open weekend, Texas is heading to Dallas for its rivalry clash with Oklahoma. Although a win would keep the Longhorns in the championship race—and that is most important, of course—Manning will drift off the Heisman radar with another tepid box score.

Devon Dampier, QB, Utah : Dampier, similarly, had an extra week to prepare for what's next—which is Kansas. Utah leads 4-0 behind Dampier, who's thrown for 896 yards, rushed for 135 and scored 11 total touchdowns.

Jadan Baugh, RB, Florida : After a sensational day in a rout of Ole Miss, Baugh and Florida had a miserable afternoon at Mizzou. In the 45-17 loss, he mustered just 30 yards on 15 touches. Still, through five games, he's racked up 613 yards and an FBS co-leading 11 touchdowns on the ground.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : Ho-hum, another comfy one. Stockton threw for 295 yards and three scores in a 38-14 win over Vanderbilt, pushing UGA to 5-0 ahead of a prime-time showdown with Alabama this Saturday.

Malachi Toney, WR, Miami : Clemson held Toney to 40 yards on five catches and a 19-yard run. Nevertheless, the 5-0 'Canes breezed to a 41-13 road victory. The major letdown was that Toney had a 58-yard touchdown called back due to a procedural penalty. Miami, off in Week 6, will return to host rival Florida State.

Julian Sayin, QB, Ohio State : Sayin completed 20-of-27 passes for 324 yards and three touchdowns in a critical 31-14 win at Iowa. Smith deserves all the praise he's receiving, but don't forget Sayin's excellence. He's produced 1,530 yards and 13 scores this season. Ohio State, 4-1, has a trip to Maryland up next.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss : The rest of the Ole Miss schedule is a gauntlet overall, but a clash with Vanderbilt starts the journey. In theory, it should be a straightforward matchup for Chambliss and the Rebels.

5. Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State

Alabama came to town and wrecked Mississippi State 56-23, neutralizing Kamario Taylor's running ability and forcing him into three turnovers. He finished with 258 hard-earned yards and three touchdowns as a passer.

So, the challenge is now the response. Taylor has an extra week to prepare for a tilt at 10th-ranked LSU, which has yielded just 5.9 yards per pass attempt.

Win there, and the Bulldogs are back on track.

Lose, however, and Taylor's gaudy numbers—1,609 offensive yards and 19 total touchdowns so far—won't carry as much weight as MSU's slipping record.

North Carolina gave Notre Dame a scare to start the second half, but CJ Carr led three methodical scoring drives to seal a 37-26 win.

The victory pushed the No. 3 Fighting Irish to 5-0. Carr has quietly met expectations along the way. He's registered a 71.0 completion rate, throwing for 1,197 yards—at 9.7 per attempt—with 13 touchdowns to one interception. Carr has also chipped in three short rushing scores.

Notre Dame is a heavy favorite at home against Stanford in Week 6, but a showdown at unbeaten, eighth-ranked BYU looms the following Saturday.

After a relatively quiet showing in Week 2's win at Kentucky, Russell has soared in the Heisman Trophy discussion.

The first-year starter has crested 300 offensive yards in three straight wins, throwing for three-plus touchdowns and running for another in each game. He totaled 301 yards and four scores at Mississippi State last weekend.

This weekend, Bama has No. 2 Georgia on the docket. Through five games, UGA's defense has ceded 5.7 yards per pass attempt—a top-10 mark nationally.

Russell is entering the biggest game of his young career on Saturday night.

Rest in peace, absurd touchdown-to-incompletion ratio.

Entering the important Week 5 clash at Clemson, Darian Mensah had tallied 14 passing scores compared to only 12 uncaught attempts. He merely went 18-of-27 for 227 yards and a touchdown in the 41-13 road blowout.

That statistical anomaly aside, the game was uncomplicated. Mensah added 27 rushing yards and a score, propelling Miami to a 5-0 record.

Miami has an open Saturday ahead, then hosts Florida State in Week 7.

We knew it was coming, but Jeremiah Smith is officially the most productive wide receiver in Ohio State history.

There's no shortage of recent superstars at the position.

In a 31-14 win at Iowa, Smith reeled in 11 passes for 206 yards and two scores. He became OSU's leader in both career receptions and touchdowns—two weeks after surpassing the program's all-time yardage mark.

Those accomplishments are nice, but they do not influence his Heisman standing.

On the other hand, Smith currently leads the FBS leaderboard with 44 catches, 823 yards and nine touchdowns. That certainly does the job.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 5
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 23-of-30, 340 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 1 yard Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Florida) Week 5 Outcome: Win (45-17)

One week after the Florida defense limited Ole Miss star Trinidad Chambliss (25/34, 298 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT) in a 52-28 win, Austin Simmons carved up the Gators, leading Missouri to a 28-point victory.

Simmons has 1,287 passing yards, with 13 touchdowns and zero interceptions this year. He ranks third in the SEC in passer rating, behind only Georgia's Gunner Stockton and Alabama's Keelon Russell.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 31-of-34, 428 yards, 5 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 26 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Colorado State) Week 5 Outcome: Win (56-26)

A 3-star transfer who spent his freshman season at Mercer University, Braden Atkinson had 3,596 yards and 34 touchdowns last season. His production has translated to the FBS level.

Oregon State has already improved on last year's 2-10 finish with a 3-2 start. Atkinson leads the nation in completions (137) and passing yards (1,848) while pacing the new-look Pac-12 in virtually every passing category.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 19-of-35, 201 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, 12 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Ball State) Week 5 Outcome: Win (39-24)

After three seasons serving as backup to DeQuan Finn and Tucker Gleason while attempting just 96 passes, John Alan Richter has stepped into the starting role.

He leads the MAC in passing yards (1,362) and passing touchdowns (13). The Rockets have won four straight since a season-opening loss on the road against Michigan State. They didn't need much from him on Saturday, as the running game piled up 352 yards and three touchdowns on 51 carries.

B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Rankings after Week 5 🔢

Week 5 Passing Stats: 10-of-18, 113 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 2 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Virginia Tech) Week 5 Outcome: Win (35-33)

The Panthers entered the latest AP poll at No. 25 after Friday night's victory over Virginia Tech, but quarterback Mason Heintschel's season ended when he suffered a torn ACL in the third quarter.

He completed 66.2 percent of his pass attempts for 1,304 yards, with 14 touchdowns and one interception prior to the injury. He was on track toward taking a significant step forward after a solid true freshman campaign.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 11-of-23, 227 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 20 carries, 149 yards, 2 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Iowa State) Week 5 Outcome: Loss (42-45)

Michael Hawkins Jr. put together another dynamic dual-threat performance on Saturday, scoring four touchdowns. He did so with his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and logging a season-high 227 passing yards.

Unfortunately, the West Virginia defense was torched for 577 yards and 45 points. The Mountaineers came out on the losing end of his strong individual performance.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 26-of-39, 238 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 10 carries, 108 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Maryland) Week 5 Outcome: Win (48-23)

The Cornhuskers are 5-0 for the first time since 2016. UNLV transfer Anthony Colandrea has proven to be a better fit for Nebraska under Matt Rhule than touted recruit Dylan Raiola was in his two years with the team.

Saturday was the first 100-yard rushing game of Colandrea's career, which is saying something after his 649-yard, 10-touchdown performance with his legs a year ago. A much tougher test awaits this weekend when Nebraska welcomes No. 7 Indiana to Lincoln.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 21-of-34, 197 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 3 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Missouri) Week 5 Outcome: Loss (17-45)

Aaron Philo was asked to throw a season-high 34 passes on Saturday after averaging 21.8 attempts through Florida's first four games. With the running game bottled up (25 carries, 42 yards), he couldn't pick up the slack and carry the load offensively.

The Gators had eight punts and a turnover on downs in a game where Missouri had 235 more yards of total offense. One of Florida's two touchdowns drives actually came with backup Tramell Jones Jr. under center to close out the game.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 25-of-32, 295 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 22 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Vanderbilt) Week 5 Outcome: Win (38-14)

After a shaky performance (14/25, 171 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT) against Oklahoma in Week 4, Gunner Stockton rebounded with a season-high 295 passing yards and his first multi-touchdown game in SEC play this year.

Stockton now leads the SEC in completion percentage (75.5) and passer rating (202.0). He has thrown 13 touchdown passes against one interception. The Bulldogs have not faced a ranked opponent yet, but that will change on Saturday when they travel to Tuscaloosa to face No. 6 Alabama.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 14-of-32, 168 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 15 carries, -62 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Florida State) Week 5 Outcome: Loss (7-38)

The Virginia offense had its worst game of the season by a significant margin on Saturday, as Beau Pribula was sacked 10 times. They finished with seven punts and four turnovers on downs.

Fingers need to be pointed in multiple directions when a team allows 10 sacks. Pribula certainly deserves his share of the blame for not finding a way to mitigate some of those losses.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 21-of-29, 234 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 15 yards, 1 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (North Carolina) Week 5 Outcome: Win (37-26)

With a season-high five total touchdowns and an impressive 72.4 percent completion rate, CJ Carr put together his best individual performance of the season on the road against the Tar Heels.

The running game still shouldered the load, with 45 carries for 241 yards and a touchdown, but Carr scored the touchdown. Next up is a matchup against a Stanford defense that allows the sixth-most passing yards per game in the country (299.8).

Week 5 Passing Stats: 20-of-30, 160 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 10 carries, -7 yards, 1 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Boston College) Week 5 Outcome: Win (25-16)

With seven touchdowns and only one turnover in the last two weeks, Kevin Jennings has done a much better job taking care of the football after turning it over five times through SMU's first three games.

He leads the ACC with 1,588 passing yards, and his 75.0 percent completion rate this year ranks fourth among FBS quarterbacks, up from 66.1 percent a year ago. After falling behind 10-6 early in the game, Jennings' three touchdowns flipped it to 25-10.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 21-of-30, 254 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 24 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (NC State) Week 5 Outcome: Loss (28-31)

After climbing to No. 16 in the AP poll during a 2-1 start, Louisville has fallen to 2-3 on the year with losses to Wake Forest and NC State in the last two weeks, dropping them out of the national picture.

Lincoln Kienholz has been one of the nation's most productive transfer quarterbacks. His 1,552 total yards rank eighth in the nation this year. His 15 total touchdowns rank third among ACC players, trailing only Darian Mensah (17) and Kevin Jennings (16).

Week 5 Passing Stats: 20-of-27, 251 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -3 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Rutgers) Week 5 Outcome: Win (47-15)

The Rutgers defense is allowing 38.5 points per game to FBS opponents this season, so Indiana's lopsided victory was the expected outcome on Saturday. Josh Hoover successfully padded his passing stats by throwing four passing touchdowns for the fourth time this year.

The TCU transfer leads the Big Ten in passing touchdowns (15) and passer rating (203.7). After tallying 24 interceptions over the last two seasons, he has yet to be picked off this year.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 18-of-33, 239 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, 50 yards, 3 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (UCF) Week 5 Outcome: Won (27-17)

Conner Weigman has five rushing touchdowns in the last two weeks, including a career-high three rushing scores in Saturday's victory against UCF. With 700 rushing yards and 11 scores on the ground a year ago, his legs have been a major weapon since he arrived at Houston as a Texas A&M transfer.

His 17 total touchdowns this season are tied with Heisman Trophy candidates Darian Mensah and Jayden Maiava for fourth-most in the nation, as he has piloted Houston to a 4-1 start and the No. 22 spot in the AP poll.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 25-of-37, 284 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 17 yards, 1 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Cincinnati) Week 5 Outcome: Win (34-7)

The Big 12 leader in passing yards (1,415) and passing touchdowns (13), Noah Fifita is in his fourth season as the starting quarterback at the University of Arizona and has led the Wildcats to a 4-1 start after a blowout win over previously undefeated Cincinnati.

He led four straight scoring drives to begin the second half, turning a 10-0 game at halftime into a convincing victory. He will line up opposite dual-threat standout Michael Hawkins Jr. in next week's matchup with West Virginia.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 16-of-22, 285 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 16 yards, 1 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Mississippi State) Week 5 Outcome: Win (56-23)

In a marquee matchup of breakout quarterbacks and undefeated SEC contenders, Keelon Russell and Alabama cruised past Kamario Taylor and Mississippi State to improve to 5-0 and climb to No. 6 in the AP poll.

After a shaky first two weeks settling in as the starting quarterback, Russell has completed 60-of-79 pass attempts for 970 yards, 10 touchdowns and zero interceptions over the last three games. He also has 107 rushing yards at 6.7 yards per carry and three more scores with his legs.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 21-of-34, 245 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -3 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Washington) Week 5 Outcome: Win (25-21)

It has been a tale of two seasons for Jayden Maiava so far, as he has cooled off after a red-hot start to the year that had him steadily climbing in the Heisman Trophy picture.

Week 0-3: 87-of-115 (75.7%), 1,173 yards, 12 TD, 1 INT Week 4-5: 44-of-76 (57.9%), 517 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT

That said, the Trojans fell behind 21-10 early in the third quarter on Saturday against Washington. He led a pair of scoring drives, along with a defensive touchdown from USC, to spark the comeback win.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 19-of-34, 258 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, -26 yards Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Alabama) Week 5 Outcome: Loss (23-56)

On his first two drives of the game on Saturday, Kamario Taylor fumbled and threw a pick-six, digging a 14-0 hole before he really had a chance to settle into the game against Alabama.

To his credit, he responded to the pick-six with a 12-play, 75-yard touchdown drive, but three turnovers, five sacks and an inconsistent passing performance overall were too much to overcome.

He injured his right leg against Missouri in Week 4 and left Saturday's game early before returning to the sideline in a walking boot. Head coach Jeff Lebby called him " day to day ," as the Bulldogs have a well-timed bye week before facing LSU on Oct. 17.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 20-of-27, 324 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, -1 yard Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Iowa) Week 5 Outcome: Win (31-14)

The Ohio State offense vs. Iowa defense matchup was one of the most compelling storylines of the Week 5 slate. The Hawkeyes secondary simply had no response to the Julian Sayin-to-Jeremiah Smith connection.

Smith hauled in 11 catches on 15 targets for 206 yards and two touchdowns. He has 44 receptions for 823 yards and nine touchdowns on the season. That standout production has helped Sayin lead the Big Ten in completion percentage (72.5) and yards per attempt (10.8) in what has been another extremely efficient season.

Week 5 Passing Stats: 18-of-27, 227 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 5 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 27 yards, 1 TD Week 5 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Clemson) Week 5 Outcome: Win (41-13)

Darian Mensah had a season-low completion percentage and failed to throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this year, but it's hard to poke too many holes in a 28-point road victory over Clemson.

Even with the good-not-great showing, Mensah still leads the nation with an absurd 84.2 percent completion rate. He has 1,438 passing yards and 15 touchdowns during Miami's undefeated start.

To keep things fresh and include breakout performers, we will re-rank the top 20 quarterbacks each week on this final slide. That will then reset the field for next week's report cards.

Quarterbacks with a Week 6 bye who are performing at a top-20 level were still included in the updated rankings to show how they stack up to the field.

However, since there will be no Week 6 performance to grade, they are presented with "***" rather than a ranking number and will not appear in next week's article.

articles.title: Nations League 2026-27: How does promotion, relegation, knockouts and Euro 2028 work?
articles.summary: With more than half of the 2026-27 Nations League group stage completed, BBC Sport looks at what will happen next in the competition.
articles.body:
England will close in on qualification for the 2026-27 Nations League quarter-finals if they beat Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday night.

Thomas Tuchel's side sit second after three matches in Group A3, with a win all but confirming their place in next March's quarter-finals.

Tuesday night will mark the final fixtures of the fourth round of group stage matches. The final two full rounds will be played in November's international break.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

Teams finishing at the top of groups in leagues B and C will earn promotion for the next Nations League cycle, while teams that finish second in a League B or League C group will face a third-place team from the league above them in a promotion/relegation play-off.

The losers of the relegation play-offs, as well as the bottom-placed finishers from groups in League A and League B will be relegated.

As the Nations League format is changing for the next cycle, taking place across 2028 and 2029, all League D teams are guaranteed promotion to League C.

Additionally, no teams from League C will be relegated at the end of this cycle.

The new format will consist of three larger leagues, meaning there will not be a League D in the next campaign.

Who will feature in the Nations League quarter-finals?

Portugal are the only side guaranteed to play in the quarter-finals at present, having won their opening four matches in Group A4.

Spain will join them from Group A3 on Tuesday, should they beat Croatia and Czech Republic fail to beat England.

If England and Spain both win on Tuesday, England would need just one point from their final two matches against Croatia and Spain next month to book their place in the last eight.

In Group A1, France and Italy sit in the top two spots. Belgium are a point behind Italy in third. Two of those three sides will advance to the quarter-finals.

It is a similar tale in Group A2. Netherlands and Greece are the top two, three points clear of Germany in third. With Serbia bottom on zero points, two of the current top three will advance.

In A4, Denmark are second and three points clear of Wales and Norway. One of the trio will join table-toppers Portugal.

The quarter-finals are played across two legs in March's international break.

The winners of each tie will advance to the semi-finals in June 2027, which are played in a one-off match across Wednesday 9 and Thursday 10 June. The final takes place on Sunday, 13 June.

While England's League A campaign has gone well so far, Wales' has been trickier.

In a tough group with Portugal, Denmark and Norway, Wales have picked up three points from four games after beating Norway 2-1 in Cardiff.

With Portugal already qualified for the last eight, Wales will need close to maximum points in their final matches against Norway and Portugal to stand any chance of making the last eight.

A third-place finish would put them in a play-off to avoid relegation in March, while coming last in the group would guarantee a drop down to League B.

Like England, Scotland have three rounds of fixtures remaining. They face Slovenia at Hampden Park on Tuesday.

Going into that tie, they are third in League B1 but only behind Slovenia on goal difference. A win for Sebastien Pocognoli's side would put them second behind Switzerland heading into the November break.

With Scotland's penultimate match coming against bottom of the table North Macedonia, wins in their next two games would all but seal a place in the top two heading into their final match against Switzerland, who are expected to clinch the automatic promotion spot.

Northern Ireland have had a successful international break with two wins, two draws and no goals conceded in their four matches in Group B2.

They sit top of the group by a point, with their remaining matches against bottom side Ukraine and second-place Hungary.

Should they beat Ukraine and Hungary fail to beat Georgia in November's first round of fixtures, they will guarantee top spot and promotion. A win for them and Hungary doing the same would mean the two sides face off in a promotion-decider in the final round of games.

The Republic of Ireland are third in Group B3 following five points from their first four matches.

Their remaining two fixtures are against the top two teams Austria and Kosovo. Wins in both would guarantee a top-two finish and would also put them in a strong position to win the group, depending on goal difference and the result of Austria's meeting with Israel.

How does the Nations League effect Euro 2028 qualifying?

Once the Nations League campaign is concluded, all 54 competing nations will be ranked based on their performance in this edition of the competition.

That ranking will have a direct impact on qualification for the 2028 European Championships, being held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The Nations League ranking will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

Regular qualifying will take place between March and November 2027, with play-offs for the remaining spots in the tournament to take place in March 2028.

As there are four co-hosts and none of them have been granted immediate qualification, the number of how many qualify will effectively determine how many play-off spots will be up for grabs.

Uefa have said that up to two places will be given to the best-ranked co-hosts that fail to qualify for the tournament via its primary qualification route.

Scenarios have already been designed for occurrences where either two, one or zero co-hosts are given entry spots.

Depending on which play-off format is required, either eight or 12 teams will enter.

A total of 24 teams will enter the European Championships, 20 of them will consist of the winners of the 12 qualifying groups and the eight best runners-up from those group.

The remaining runners-up will enter the play-offs, alongside the Nations League group winners from League A, League B and League C that failed to finish in the top two of their Euro 2028 qualifying group.

If extra teams are required, the best-ranked League D group winner will enter the play-offs.

Any additional play-off spots that become available after that will filter down to the next-highest ranked Nations League finishers until the play-off spots are filled.

articles.title: Gordon: "He tirado muchos desmarques en mi carrera que nadie veía, pero ahora Pedri sí los ve"
articles.standfirst: El inglés, muy feliz en sus primeros meses como culé
articles.summary: El inglés, muy feliz en sus primeros meses como culé
articles.body: gordon fue el primer fichaje del Barcelona el pasado verano y el inglés está muy feliz en esta nueva etapa como culé. En una entrevista a la revista oficial del club, el extremo elogia el juego de sus compañeros y reconoce que el bloque tiene calidad para ganar todos los títulos. Además, explica que Eric García y Olmo, que hablan un inglés perfecto, le han ayudado mucho en su adaptación. "Lo que representa el Barça para mí es que el rival toque el balón lo menos posible. Ahora también tenemos agresividad. Me he adaptado bien porque es un juego muy similar al Newcastle. La principal diferencia con la Premier es la intensidad, aquí es todo es más pausado y basado en el control y la posesión. He hecho muchos desmarques a lo largo de mi carrera que nadie veía, pero ahora Pedri los ve. Quiero ganar todos los títulos y tenemos plantilla para lograrlo", resalta el internacional inglés. Gordon tiene claro cuál es el mejor Barça. "El de Pep Guardiola, el que ganó la Liga de Campeones con jugadores como Xavi e Iniesta. Mi jugador favorito de la historia del Barça, dejando de lado a Messi, es Luis Suárez. Soy un gran aficionado del Liverpool y ya era mi favorito allí junto a Gerrard", dice. El extremo tilda de agradable, abierta y cálida su llegada al Barcelona. "Eric García me ha ayudado mucho porque habla un inglés perfecto y Dani Olmo, también. Entiendo el castellano pero cuando hablan muy rápido entre ellos me cuesta más seguirles", asevera. Precisamente, Gordon sorprendió en sus presentación dirigiéndose en español a los medios de comunicación. Por otro lado, el azulgrana está muy agradecido al cariño que recibe por parte de la grada desde el primer día. "Esta afición ha admirado a jugadores como Messi, Ronaldinho, Luis Suárez y mucho de los mejores jugadores de la historia y no pensaba sentirme tan apreciado desde el primer momento. En el Newcastle me pasó algo parecido, la gente me veía como un jugador rápido, pero descubrió otros aspectos de mi juego", explica. De hecho, considera que en este arranque aún tiene la asignatura pendiente del gol. Por último, destaca la figura de Hansi Flick, sin olvidarse de todos y cada uno de los entrenadores que ha tenido en su carrera, porque le ha dado la oportunidad de vivir un sueño. Además, deja claro que no siente presión extra. "No creo mucho en la presión, es algo que te creas tú mismo, en tu mente. Si de pequeño no sentías presión, ahora tampoco debes sentirla. Yo disfruto jugando", dice.

articles.title: Alaba: "Hablé con muchos amigos que han jugado en Italia, como Modric o Ribéry"
articles.standfirst: El defensor austriaco fue presentado con Udinese
articles.summary: El defensor austriaco fue presentado con Udinese
articles.body: David Alaba, presentado este martes como jugador del Udinese, reveló haber hablado con amigos que juegan o jugaron en Italia, como Luka Modric o Franck Ribéry, y afirmó que no le pesa desempeñar el papel de "hermano mayor" en el club italiano ya que también lo desempeñó en el Bayern Múnich o en el Real Madrid. "No es la primera vez en mi carrera que voy a asumir el papel de hermano mayor, ya me ha ocurrido antes. Soy una persona a la que siempre le ha gustado asumir responsabilidades, también en la selección austríaca, donde soy uno de los jugadores más experimentados", dijo el defensa central, ganador con 38 títulos durante su carrera en Alemania y en España. "Personalmente, siempre he intentado desempeñar ese papel, también en el Bayern Múnich y en el Real Madrid, así que no es nada nuevo para mí", agregó. Alaba, que llega al Udinese tras su etapa en el Real Madrid, explicó que su decisión estuvo muy vinculada al proyecto deportivo que le presentó el técnico del conjunto italiano, Kosta Runjaic. "Hablé principalmente con el entrenador. Él me convenció del proyecto que hay aquí y me tomé el tiempo necesario para tomar esta decisión. Con el tiempo, me convencí de que este era el camino correcto para mí, porque creo que es el paso adecuado para mi carrera, tanto a nivel personal como profesional. Por eso elegí el Udinese", explicó. El internacional austríaco, que no juega un partido oficial desde hace varios meses debido a sus problemas físicos y que alegó que por el momento no renuncia a la selección, aseguró que se encuentra preparado para volver a competir después de haberse incorporado la pasada semana a los entrenamientos con el equipo. "Me siento muy bien, me siento preparado para jugar. La semana pasada empecé a entrenar con el equipo y me vino muy bien. Hemos trabajado mucho y durante las últimas semanas también he entrenado mucho, así que puedo decir que estoy bien y que me siento muy bien", señaló. Sobre su posición en la pizarra, Alaba explicó que en los últimos años se ha asentado como defensa central, aunque mantiene su habitual "polivalencia". "En los últimos años he jugado principalmente como defensa central y personalmente creo que es la posición en la que puedo rendir mejor, pero también puedo jugar en otras posiciones", subrayó. Alaba se mostró además ilusionado con la oportunidad de disputar la competición italiana, un torneo "con una calidad muy alta". "Es una de las mejores ligas del planeta, de Europa, y estoy realmente feliz de poder vivir una experiencia aquí", recalcó. Alaba se formó en las categorías inferiores del Austria Viena, y a los 16 años fue fichado por el Bayern Munich, con quien conquistó dos Champions, dos Mundiales de Clubes, dos Supercopas de Europa y diez Bundesligas, entre otros. Después jugó en el conjunto madridista, donde levantó dos Ligas de Campeones, dos Mundiales de Clubes, dos Supercopas de Europa, dos Ligas, una Copa del Rey y dos Supercopas de España.

articles.title: James McClean: Ex-Republic of Ireland international hits out at Derry City treatment amid dispute
articles.summary: Derry City player James McClean hits out at his treatment by Derry City amid an ongoing contract dispute with the club.
articles.body:
James McClean says he cannot "understand or accept" how he has been treated by Derry City amid an ongoing contract dispute with the club.

In a statement released on the Professional Footballers' Association of Ireland (PFAI) website, the former Republic of Ireland international describes attempts by the League of Ireland club to terminate his contract as "incomprehensible" and says he will decide himself when is the right time to retire.

The 37-year-old insists he is still fit and available to play "when called upon" despite being left out of the squad by interim manager Mark Connolly.

McClean, who said the past few months have been "one of the most difficult periods of my life", did apologise for some "misjudged" actions on his part over recent months, adding that "his frustrations should have remained in-house".

He returned to his hometown club from Wrexham in the close-season in January but has not been included in a match-day squad since the Candystripes' Uefa Conference League defeat by Rijeka in early July.

Connolly 'sticking with same squad' amid McClean absence

McClean shares discontent with Derry City return

Reports have indicated in recent months that Derry attempted to terminate McClean's contract because of persistent injuries, a matter alluded to in Tuesday's statement by the PFAI.

The statement says that Derry had attempted to invoke Section 18 of the Standard Players Contract, which permits them to terminate a contract with six months' notice when a player is deemed to have a "permanent incapacity", as confirmed by an independent physician.

"For any club to feel it is OK to attempt to terminate a player's contract without any due process or just cause is incomprehensible, and it sets a dangerous precedent for every player in this league," said McClean.

"I am not permanently incapacitated, or anything even remotely close to that. I am capable of contributing and doing well in the League of Ireland. I train as hard and give as much as anyone.

"I will decide when I retire. Nobody else will make that decision for me. When that time comes, my body will tell me. This is my life and my career. I deserve the same duty of care and fairness given to the majority of other players at Derry City FC."

The PFAI gave further information on the nature and extent of the player's injury.

"In short, James has had a hip injury which had been causing intermittent issues for him. This has caused him to miss some games and occasional training sessions," the statement read.

"He has sought medical treatment for this and is currently fit and well.

"He has trained fully for the last nine weeks and has made himself available for selection. He recently played in an internal match arranged by the club. He believes he can help the team and has not been provided with a satisfactory reason for being left out of the squad."

Timing of statement 'frustrating' - Connolly

Speaking to BBC Sport NI on Tuesday, Connolly admitted the timing of the statement in the build-up to Saturday's FAI Cup semi-final against Galway United (15:00 BST) was "frustrating".

"It's disappointing, not for me, you just get on and do your job," said Connolly.

"The biggest thing is there's lads in that dressing room that have not played in a cup semi-final before. It's a big week for them, their families and all that.

"It's frustrating but again my full focus now is on making sure the players are ready for Saturday and making sure we go to Galway and give a good account of ourselves."

In a statement, Derry City said it was not notified about the PFAI and McClean's statement prior to its publication.

"The Club welcomes James' acknowledgement that some of his recent actions were misjudged and that his frustrations should have remained in-house," the club said.

"At all times, the Club has sought to resolve this internal matter privately. Out of respect for confidentiality and the fact that this dispute involves sensitive medical details regarding James' hip condition, the Club have previously refrained from making any public statement on the matter.

"While the PFAI and James have chosen to publicise selective elements of the medical advice received, the Club does not propose to comment further on James' current medical condition."

Derry City added they are "fully aware of the obligations it owes to all contracted players".

"All squad members who are deemed fully fit remain available for selection. Ultimately, matchday selection remains the sole prerogative of the management team, acting in conjunction with guidance from our medical staff."

The club said it will make no further comment as they prepare for Saturday's FAI Cup semi-final against Galway United (15:00 BST).

articles.title: Way-Too-Early Erling Haaland Landing Spots Amid Transfer Rumors
articles.summary: After Manchester City were found guilty of 114 charges relating to Premier League financial rule breaches, several questions remain.
articles.body:
After Manchester City were found guilty of 114 charges relating to Premier League financial rule breaches, several questions remain.

With the eight-time league champions having lodged an appeal, the most pressing question is whether those charges will stick. If that appeal fails, exactly what punishment will be handed down will become the biggest concern for City, who have maintained their innocence throughout the proceedings.

Given the strength of the Premier League's statement on the charges, in which the word "sham" was used five times, it is fair to assume that any punishment will be severe enough to potentially lead to relegation. After that, the biggest remaining questions will focus on the futures of their biggest stars, with none more intriguing than Erling Haaland's.

The 26-year-old has scored 169 goals in 205 appearances for City and has a contract in Manchester until 2034, but he would surely press for an exit if relegation is confirmed. In a worst-case scenario, it may even be impossible to keep him while complying with financial rules.

So, what are his options? Below are his five most likely destinations, with ambition, spending power, and the need for a striker as the chief considerations.

There is, of course, the possibility that a club in Saudi Arabia or a similar league could come up with enough money to turn Haaland's head. But there is no slide discussing that possibility because (1) it quite simply isn't interesting and (2) it still seems unlikely that the guy who used to drive around listening to the Champions League theme music would give up the opportunity to play in the competition for a few sacks of cash.

If you think you have a better idea, though, be sure to leave your suggestion in the B/R App comments.

Barcelona looked to have a glaring need in attack this summer. Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres departed for Major League Soccer and Paris Saint-Germain, respectively, and widely reported interest in Atlético Madrid's Julián Álvarez did not materialize.

While Gabriel Jesus did arrive from Arsenal, there was still a significant question mark over the club's plans at centre-forward, both for this season and beyond. The answer to that question has been to play former star winger Raphinha centrally, and the results have been impressive.

The Brazilian has scored 14 goals in eight appearances this season, while Barcelona have won those eight games and scored 36 goals in total. This is a small sample size, though, and Barcelona manager Hansi Flick would surely still welcome the idea of incorporating Haaland into this attack.

The deal would also see the big forward join up with Lamine Yamal to form probably the most exciting attacking partnership in Europe, putting Barcelona right in the frame as Champions League favorites.

Not really. They have Kylian Mbappe up front, and the Frenchman has been in decent form with eight goals in eight games this season. He's also joined in attack by Vinícius Júnior, who signed a new contract in the summer, and $159 million signing Yan Diomande is waiting in the wings to take on a bigger role as well.

Could adding yet another star in attack also potentially upset the balance of a squad that looks awfully top-heavy?

Good point. Mbappé certainly seems to want to be the focal point of the team, which is arguably a fair request for a man of his talents. Adding Haaland would also make Diomande a likely reserve and push either Mbappé or Vinícius out to the right side of the attack, where neither has looked entirely comfortable before.

So, there's no way Real Madrid would be interested, right?

That would be the logical conclusion, yes. But logic doesn't exist in the halls of the Santiago Bernabéu. All that matters is that the biggest stars in the world play there; the details can be figured out later, typically after a slew of the world's best managers have failed to do so. And then, eventually, the team adds to its record-setting 15 European titles, the ultimate justification for all the chaos that preceded that glory.

The team would likely need to be remodeled around him, but Haaland feels as obvious a Real Madrid target as anyone else potentially on the market. The move would also reunite him with former Borussia Dortmund teammate Jude Bellingham, and if Mbappé can be factored in as well, this would be a thrilling attack to watch.

Bayern Munich may not currently need a striker. Harry Kane scored 61 goals last season and is a serious contender to win the Ballon d'Or as the world's player of the year. Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg has also reported that the Englishman has agreed in principle to a new contract until 2029.

But at 33, it would be fair to question how much longer Kane can remain at the top of his game. Even if he is able to stave off Father Time, though, the most exciting aspect of this possibility could actually be Kane and Haaland playing together.

The former Tottenham Hotspur man has become an elite-level playmaker in Munich, in addition to his goalscoring exploits, often dropping out of the forward line to receive the ball under pressure and pinging it into space for more athletic teammates to run onto. What if he could continue fleshing out that creative side of his game, with Haaland as a potential target for those raking forward passes?

While there would likely have to be trade-offs in Bayern's intense defensive system to accommodate the two strikers, the upside of such an approach could make them almost impossible to stop in attack.

As the reigning two-time European champions, Paris Saint-Germain would be unfairly positioned to add Haaland. However, it could also be a risk to incorporate yet another superstar forward into an attack that has only really taken off after adopting a team-first approach.

Kylian Mbappé's departure for Madrid in 2024 saw Ousmane Dembélé take his place as the focal point of the team's attack, with the latter's defensive work key in setting the tone for the energetic style that has seen Luis Enrique's team roll to consecutive European titles.

PSG have been down the road of acquiring stars when it arguably didn't make sense to do so, and it led them to an expensive and futile chase for European glory until the past two seasons.

At some point, though, teams will surely start to figure out better ways to nullify this attack. It may even already be happening. Although it's early, the Parisiens have already drawn two and lost one of their five league games.

Haaland would provide more of a goalscoring threat than Dembele or the newly acquired Ferran Torres, and his size and athleticism could unlock an even more devastating element to PSG's attack that we haven't seen yet.

Darth Vader and Luke Skywalker. Professor X and Magneto. Rocky and Apollo Creed. Erling Haaland and Gabriel Magalhães?

If cinema has taught us anything, it's that when enemies have to team up, it can be pretty cool. The thought of suddenly having to support Haaland after being rage-baited by him for years might send a shiver down the spines of Gabriel and Arsenal fans alike, but North London is the only destination that makes sense if the three-time Premier League Golden Boot winner is to stay in England.

No other team can offer the combination of an obvious need in attack and the clear ability to compete for the biggest honours domestically and in Europe. Liverpool have two strikers who cost in excess of $90 million, while Chelsea and Manchester United still have questions to answer regarding how ambitious they actually are.

Arsenal have spent the summer pursuing Vinícius Júnior and Julián Álvarez, as widely reported. It's clear the forward line is where they want to make their next big addition, and Haaland's physicality would provide the attacking boost the Gunners likely had in mind when they signed Viktor Gyökeres last summer.

articles.title: Krystian Bielik: Cardiff City defender banned over Portsmouth incident
articles.summary: The Football Association bans Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik for two games and fines him £10,000 after he admitted a case of misconduct involving a Portsmouth fan.
articles.body:
The Football Association (FA) has banned Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik for two games and fined him £10,000 after he admitted a case of misconduct.

The 28-year-old Poland international was involved in an altercation involving Portsmouth fans during Cardiff's 2-0 Championship defeat at Fratton Park on Saturday, 5 September.

A Hampshire Police investigation into the flashpoint concluded that no further action was needed on its part over the incident, although as part of the resolution Bielik provided an apology.

Bielik is now set to miss the Championship trip to Blackburn Rovers on Saturday, followed by the home game against Watford on Tuesday, 13 October.

The FA charge stated that: "It was alleged that the player acted in an improper manner around the 71st minute of the fixture.

"Krystian Bielik subsequently admitted the charge. An independent Regulatory Commission imposed these sanctions following a hearing, and the written reasons for its decisions will be published in due course."

Latest Portsmouth news, analysis and fan views

Bielik was involved in a physical altercation with a fan as he went to retrieve a ball from the crowd late in the second half.

Several Portsmouth supporters made gestures that indicated they believed the fan had been grabbed by the throat.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy claimed afterwards that Bielik "got slapped in the face", while clips circulating on social media appeared to show the Poland international grabbing a young fan around his upper body.

In the aftermath, another fan threw a ball at the head of Cardiff defender Perry Ng. Both supporters were ejected from the stadium.

After the game, Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho apologised to Cardiff City's players.

In the days that followed and having been shown the footage, Mousinho said he was "absolutely furious" at the position he says he was put in over the incident.

articles.title: Kristian Shevchenko: Son of Andriy Shevchenko signs for non-league side
articles.summary: Kristian Shevchenko, son of Ballon d'Or winner Andriy Shevchenko, signs for seventh-tier club Sholing FC.
articles.body:
Kristian Shevchenko, the son of Ballon d'Or winner and Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko, has signed for seventh-tier club Sholing FC.

The 19-year-old has joined the Boatmen on a permanent deal following spells in Chelsea, Tottenham and Watford's academies.

He was most recently at Championship club Watford, playing for their under-21s team, but was released in May.

Southampton-based Sholing have some big names involved in the running of the club, with Premier League players Levi Colwill and Matt Targett both playing a role in their growth.

Chelsea and England defender Colwill is associate director and community ambassador while Hull City's Targett has a younger brother Brad who plays for the Southern League Premier Division South club.

Manager Paul Doswell said a recent change in transfer strategy at the club was behind the signing.

"The move came from some of our coaching staff and their links in academy football," he told BBC Radio Solent.

"We spoke to Kristian last week and he's very keen to be part of the model here and see if he can get in the team and progress his football career with us.

"We've got a real way forward that we're going to sign the best young players that get released from pro clubs and give them a chance to play in non-league football.

"We'll then hopefully improve them as they're with us and get them back playing in the professional league."

Former Ukraine striker Andriy played for AC Milan, Chelsea and Dynamo Kyiv during his career, before retiring in 2012.

He won the 2003 Champions League with Milan and clinched the Ballon d'Or in 2004.

articles.title: Germán 'Mono' Burgos: "Lamine Yamal es nuestro Messi y va a marcar una época"
articles.standfirst: El ex guardameta y entrenador argentino, protagonista en 'Directo MARCA'
articles.summary: El ex guardameta y entrenador argentino, protagonista en 'Directo MARCA'
articles.body: Germán ‘Mono’ Burgos repasó la actualidad del fútbol en Directo MARCA y dejó varias reflexiones de mucho peso sobre Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal, el Atlético de Madrid y Diego Simeone. Sobre el argentino, el ex guardameta fue rotundo al describir lo que suponía enfrentarse a él: "Es imparable. Es una cosa que no llegas ni a darle una patada. Ese es el problema. Porque no lo puedes detener". Burgos destacó además la dimensión de su carrera y aseguró que Messi "ha sido y es uno de los mejores del mundo, sin ninguna duda". Burgos también se rindió ante Lamine Yamal, al que colocó directamente en la estela del astro argentino. Preguntado por si el joven azulgrana puede ser considerado "nuestro Messi" para el fútbol español, no dudó: "Para mí sí". Y fue todavía más lejos al pronosticar que el internacional español "va a marcar una época en el fútbol español y en el fútbol mundial". El argentino explicó que, aunque juegue en otra posición, Lamine tiene ese punto diferencial que recuerda a los grandes genios: "Cuando la agarra Lamine, sabes que algo va a pasar". Sobre el Atlético de Madrid, Burgos ve al equipo rojiblanco con argumentos para pelear por todo, aunque puso el foco en una condición indispensable: ganar los grandes partidos. "Siempre tiene buenos equipos el Atleti, siempre y buenos jugadores", afirmó. Pero también lanzó un aviso que resume la dificultad del reto: "¿Es fácil ganar al Real Madrid? No es fácil, muchachos". Para Burgos, el conjunto de Simeone debe seguir acumulando victorias importantes para llegar con opciones al final de la temporada. Más incógnita dejó cuando fue preguntado por el futuro de Diego Simeone y por si esta podría ser la última temporada del técnico argentino en el Metropolitano. Burgos, que compartió muchos años de vestuario y banquillo con el Cholo, evitó hacer pronósticos: "No sé, la verdad que no sé porque no sé cómo está la parte interna". Eso sí, dejó claro que, mientras siga en el Atlético, Simeone continuará peleando hasta el último día. "Yo no hablaría de un final anticipado, seguro", sentenció. Y todavía hubo tiempo para un último guiño a Messi. Al ser preguntado por el próximo Balón de Oro y por la posibilidad de que el argentino pudiera conquistar un noveno galardón, Burgos volvió a colocarle por delante de cualquier otro candidato: "Por supuesto que lo podría ganar Lamine, pero antes a Messi". El ex portero consideró que el argentino se merece ese reconocimiento por su trayectoria y por todo lo que ha dado al fútbol: "El chiquitito se lo merece también, 39 años, muchachos". Una declaración de intenciones que resume perfectamente la admiración de Burgos por una leyenda que, según sus palabras, sigue siendo capaz de estar por encima de todos.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026: Waiver wire, Week 5 edition
articles.summary: Wading into the free agent pool for roster help
articles.body:
Welcome to the Fantasy Football Waiver Wire for Week 5.

Injuries continue to be a major menace for fantasy managers in 2026, and Week 4 continued that trend as a number of fantasy starters were either inactive or left games with injuries during the Week 4 games. It's starting to feel like a war of attrition out there.

In addition to that annoyance, we've got Bye weeks to contend with. The waiver wire can offer some assistance although this isn't a great week for free agent adds. Still, help is there for those who need it, and that includes some intriguing stashes who might be difference-makers later in the season.

The Process : Each week, I try to identify the top Waiver Wire targets and evaluate the short- and long-term prospects of those players. I also do my best to reveal which players who are coming off a big week are fool's gold. Finally, I look at streamers who might help you in a pinch (this is usually more important during bye weeks).

Some players discussed won't be available in your league. I try to list players who are available in more than 50% of leagues. But what does that even mean? A 10-team league with six bench spots will have a much larger Free Agent pool than a 14-team league with eight. Most leagues fall somewhere in between. This isn't "one size fits all." By way of example, I won't list Bryce Young, Kyle Monangai, Braelon Allen , Kendre Miller , Woody Marks, Khalil Shakir, or Juwan Johnson this week, among others who probably aren't available in any of your leagues.

If you need a second QB in a Superflex format, or a temporary starter in a one-QB format, I'll list the same three graybeards who I named last week: Kirk Cousins , Aaron Rodgers, and Geno Smith . Cousins is playing very well and has put up multiple TDs in every game, and at least 20 fantasy points in three straight weeks. The Jets offense couldn't get on the field last week, but Geno has been decent. Rodgers is having a mini-resurgence, and has a very favorable upcoming schedule (Colts, Bucs, Saints, Browns, Bengals).

Need a Week 5 streamer at QB? I'll give you three matchup-based names to consider.

Jacoby Brissett gets the Lions this week. I'll say that again to make sure you didn't miss it. Arizona plays Detroit this week. Did you see the Lions' defense on Sunday night? Well, nobody did, because they don't actually play any defense. That performance wasn't an anomaly. They're that bad against the pass. Brissett is a solid streamer in Week 5, and for that matter so are C.J. Stroud (@TEN), who is a different QB when Nico Collins is in the lineup, and Jameis Winston (@WAS), who gave fans the full Jameis experience last Sunday (3 TDs, 2 INTs) and who also faces another of the league's worst secondaries this week.

I guess I have to say something about Deshaun Watson . He's playing well and while it hasn't been outstanding for fantasy, he should be rostered in two-QB leagues. His matchup this week (NYJ) is just so-so, as teams have been running all over them.

Finally, Jalon Daniels is going to struggle and turn the ball over. He's also going to run, and he should get a little better at the whole passing the football thing with more starts. Add him at your own risk – but if you need help, it looks like he'll get a bunch more starts while Baker Mayfield's thumb heals.

Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby both left Sunday's game with injuries, and Bigsby is headed to IR. Will Shipley is definitely in for significantly more work and could actually be the lead back if Barkley, who has been in and out of the lineup the last few weeks, misses time. The Eagles' offense is a mess, but volume is volume. Shipley is my top add this week.

Let's talk about the Seahawks, who just put Jadarian Price on IR.

Zach Charbonnet's practice window opened, meaning he could be nearing a return. He's rostered in more than 50% of leagues but is worth stashing if he's available.

If you need more immediate help, Emanuel Wilson is coming off an excellent performance (24 touches, 120 total yards, two total TDs) and looks like the Seahawks' back to roster for the near-term. He could have value for the duration of the season, but this is a very hard backfield to handicap longer-term, and especially with the team signing Joe Mixon to the practice squad (I don't expect much from him, but it muddies the waters).

A few other names to think about, if you're in need and/or want some depth that could pop: Keaton Mitchell (15 touches this past week), Austin Ekeler , Tyler Allgeier , Tyler Goodson , Brian Robinson, Jr., and Mike Washington, Jr.

Tyreek Hill got scooped up in a lot of leagues over the last two weeks, and now there's a report that the Chiefs, who lost both Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton to injuries on Sunday, have reached out to his agent. Hill is at least a month away from potentially playing, so this is speculative in multiple ways. But if you've got the space, why not?

Both Denzel Boston and K.C. Concepcion should be rostered. It's true: Watson is playing well, and the two rookies look good and are getting plenty of chances to make plays.

I think Darius Cooper (who came out of nowhere to score two TDs Sunday, on just three catches) is probably fool's gold, and I really don't like how the Eagles' offense looks. I'd pass on him for other names, but I get it if you want to chase that performance while Philly is missing so many weapons. I prefer Dontayvion Wicks there.

As for players who can help you right now, Keon Coleman is coming off a big game but he has fooled us before. Still, with D.J. Moore re-aggravating his shoulder, Coleman is worth considering.

The Romeo Doubs breakout game finally happened – and I bet almost nobody started him. Some people dropped him already, so he could be on waiver wires and especially in shallower leagues. It's hard to trust, but if Drake Maye is out of his funk, Doubs could be serviceable, at least until A.J. Brown returns.

Jordyn Tyson could be back as early as Week 7, but with the Saints having a Bye in Week 8, I think Week 9 is a more likely target. He's worth stashing and especially if you can keep him in an IR spot.

Need receiver depth? I'll repeat a bunch of names I've listed in recent weeks, together with some new ones: Roman Wilson , Malik Washington, Tre Harris, Khalif Raymond , Chris Bell , Antonio Williams , and Tre Harris .

Cyrus Allen had a lot of preseason hype. He's worth stashing given Kansas City's receiver injuries, and with the 4-0 Chiefs on a Bye this week he should be easy to nab.

Have you heard of Dohnte Meyers ? Well, you might not hear about him, if Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and/or Tee Higgins (abductor strain) are able to play this week. But if either or both aren't, he's an attractive streamer (@MIA) for this week and possibly longer (CIN has a Bye in week 6). Someone has to catch passes from Joe Burrow. Speaking of which…

Mike Gesicki is a great option with the two starting receivers ailing. Even when both are healthy, he has value catching passes from Burrow, although like most tight ends outside of the elite options his production isn't consistent week-to-week.

Others to consider if you need help: Michael Mayer (Brock Bowers is a WR; Mayer is playing a ton of snaps and you see the production), Darren Waller (who is on a Bye this week), Brenton Strange , and Tyler Higbee .

That's all I've got. Good luck with your waiver claims!

We'll see if the Yellow Jackets used the bye week to figure some things out after a rough start to the season.

articles.title: Nick Pope’s Newcastle Story Is Ending. Nobody’s Quite Sure How Yet
articles.summary: Just over 18 months ago, Nick Pope was Newcastle’s goalkeeper when the club finally ended its 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. Today, he’s third choice, h...
articles.body:
Just over 18 months ago, Nick Pope was Newcastle's goalkeeper when the club finally ended its 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. Today, he's third choice, hasn't played a competitive minute all season, and the only real question left is whether his Newcastle career ends in four months or closes out properly next summer. Even that much isn't settled yet.

Pope's drop down the pecking order isn't really a mystery. Newcastle signed Lukas Hornicek for £25.7 million to become its new first-choice goalkeeper, while Ewen Jaouen arrived as another long-term option in the same window. A dip in form over recent seasons made Pope available for sale this past summer, but no move materialized before deadline day.

He has been linked with clubs including Ipswich Town and Celtic at different points, but those links never developed into a completed transfer. For now, Pope remains at Newcastle with a contract that runs until next summer.

The Reporting Keeps Shifting, and That's Worth Being Honest About

Depending on which week you check, Pope's situation has been described differently by people in the known. Earlier reporting suggested he was open to exploring a January move. More recent accounts point the other way, describing him as prioritizing free agency next summer and increasingly likely to simply see out his contract.

That doesn't mean a January departure is off the table. But the picture has changed, particularly with Jaouen's own fitness proving unreliable enough that Newcastle may not want to thin out its goalkeeping depth midway through the season. Jaissle himself has only said that any decision involves the player and his representatives as much as the club, which isn't exactly a signal either way.

Why Newcastle Might Actually Want Him to Stay

There's a practical argument for keeping Pope around that has nothing to do with sentiment.

If Jaouen's injury troubles continue, Newcastle's alternative to Hornicek as cover becomes considerably less experienced. Letting an experienced, Champions League-tested goalkeeper walk in January for a modest fee, only to leave the club exposed at the position during the second half of the season, is the kind of risk clubs generally try to avoid — even with a player who clearly isn't part of the long-term plan anymore.

Pope may no longer be Newcastle's preferred goalkeeper, but that doesn't make him useless. There is still value in having a proven Premier League goalkeeper available when the squad's other options aren't fully reliable.

What This Actually Says About the Rebuild

Pope's situation is really a small, human-scale version of the larger story Newcastle have been living through — a squad built around one era quietly giving way to another, player by player, even when the departures aren't dramatic enough to make headlines on their own.

Some exits come with transfer fees, announcements and plenty of fanfare. Pope's will likely be different. He's a 34-year-old goalkeeper whose place in the squad has already been taken, but whose experience still gives Newcastle a reason to keep him around.

Whenever his Newcastle career finally ends, it will mark the quiet conclusion of a significant chapter. Pope was there when Newcastle ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. He was one of the goalkeepers who helped turn the club from a side hoping to return to the top into one competing on the biggest stages in Europe.

Now, he's waiting for his next move. Whether that comes in January or next summer, the ending is getting closer. The only thing still genuinely unresolved is the when.

Arsenal believes he could make an immediate impact in north London. His experience at the highest level would also strengthen the squad as the Gunners compete for major honours.

Barcelona has previously been unwilling to allow Kounde to leave, but its position has now changed. Sport reports that the Catalan club is open to selling the defender if a suitable offer arrives.

The club would prefer to retain him, but it is no longer treating him as untouchable. A substantial proposal could therefore persuade Barcelona to sanction his departure.

That development is encouraging for Arsenal, which has maintained its interest in the Frenchman. The Gunners could now explore a deal if they believe Kounde is available at an acceptable price.

Kounde's arrival could signal that Arsenal intends to sell either Ben White or Jurrien Timber. The Frenchman can operate at right back and centre back, giving Mikel Arteta another high-quality defensive option.

He could also become an immediate starter at the Emirates. His experience with Barcelona and France means he would not need much time to adjust to the demands of playing for a leading club.

Arsenal must still meet Barcelona's financial expectations, as the Catalans will not allow Kounde to leave for a modest fee. Other clubs may also compete for his signature if his availability becomes clear.

The Gunners will therefore need to act decisively. If they complete the transfer, Kounde could strengthen their defence and provide the quality and versatility they want in every position.

articles.title: Lionel Messi's final Argentina stats: Games, goals, assists, trophies, and more after international retirement
articles.summary: Widely considered the greatest player in the history of the game, superstar Lionel Messi has finally brought his international career to an end at 39 years o...
articles.body:
Widely considered the greatest player in the history of the game, superstar Lionel Messi has finally brought his international career to an end at 39 years old.

In the aftermath of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Messi announced he would not play again for Argentina, with the death of his father Jorge a large factor in his decision to hang up his Albiceleste boots.

For a long time, Messi's international career was blighted by an inability to win major international trophies, but by the time it was all said and done, he had lifted just about every single trophy there is to win in the entire sport.

The Sporting News brings you a final look at his international career, as the Argentina legend cemented his legacy on both an individual and team level.

All data either via Transfermarkt or MessivsRonaldo.app unless otherwise specified or linked.

After the final match against Benin, Lionel Messi finishes his international career having played 208 games for Argentina.

The legendary footballer made his debut on August 17, 2005 as a second-half substitute against Hungary, in a match Argentina would win 2-1, but Messi received a red card just a minute after entering the field.

21 years later, his final match would come on October 6, 2026, leaving him second all-time in international matches played on the men's side. He is second only to the 234 caps owned by Cristiano Ronaldo , with Luka Modric behind him in third with 204. It's possible — likely, even, that Modric catches him soon.

In those games, he has played 17,112 minutes throughout his career.

Lionel Messi concludes his international career with 125 goals scored for his country.

That is the second-most in the history of the game, behind only the 146 for Cristiano Ronaldo and above the 108 for Ali Daeli of Iran.

His first career international goal came against Croatia in a 3-2 friendly defeat on March 1, 2006. He would score his final goal against Egypt in a 3-2 victory at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, aiding in a furious comeback that saw Argentina respond from down 2-0, with Messi's goal the equalizer in the 83rd minute, before Enzo Fernandez won it in the 92nd minute.

Messi has the second-most goals in World Cup history, briefly breaking Mario Gotze's record in the 2026 competition before being passed just days later by Kylian Mbappe. He also has the most goals in CONMEBOL World Cup qualifying, and has the joint-fifth-most goals in Copa America history.

He has scored 11 international hat-tricks, which is the most international triples in FIFA men's history, and is one shy of American superstar Alex Morgan for the most on either the men's or women's side.

While assists can sometimes be a disputed statistic, it is largely held that Lionel Messi has 65 assists for his country, believed to be the most ever in international football .

For a long time, American forward Landon Donovan held the record for the most assists in international football with 58, but Messi passed him during the 2025 calendar year.

Neymar is third with 57, just one below Donovan.

Messi's first career international assist actually came before his first goal, as he fed Juan Roman Riquelme for the first goal of a 3-0 friendly win over Qatar on November 16, 2005, just a few months before he would score his first ever international goal. It was maybe the easiest assist of them all, as he simply touched the ball to Riquelme in midfield before the striker buried a ludicrous long-range effort that bounced in after a poor dive by the goalkeeper saw him fail to keep it out.

One of the most fascinating things about Lionel Messi's international career was how, for much of his time with Argentina, he was thought of as the best player never to win a major international trophy. For a long stretch of his career, Messi fell just short of many international trophies.

Then, in 2021, that all changed as a 33-year-old Messi led Argentina to the Copa America title, beating Brazil in the final.

From there, he would go on a generational run of international dominance, winning the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the 2022 Finalissima, and the 2024 Copa America, giving him four major international trophies .

Messi also won an Olympic gold medal in 2008, but that is considered a youth tournament, and as such is not considered a major international accomplishment.

* Not considered a major international trophy at the senior level.

Pascual se mostró "muy contento" por ser al autor del gol del triunfo pese a jugar sólo los últimos minutos, algo que ya ocurrió en la tercera jornada ante el Córdoba. "Es difícil jugar un partido y luego el otro no, pero lo que importa es la confianza en uno mismo. Yo confío mucho en mí y sé las condiciones que tengo", comentó.
