articles.title: End of an era as Messi prepares to hang up Argentina boots
articles.summary: Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina's sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in...
articles.body:
Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina's sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in a stadium with a name to match his legacy: Monumental.

Some 85,000 spectators will be present to watch the 39-year-old idol perform his wizardry in a friendly against Benin that brings down the curtain on his 21-year international career.

Millions more will follow the action in South America's largest stadium, Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental, on TV.

The most-capped player in Argentine history is hanging up his boots two-and-a-half months after losing the World Cup final to Spain.

"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.

On Monday, he took part in his last training session with the team at the complex that bears his name in the Buenos Aires suburb of Ezeiza.

"I believe Messi gave everything, absolutely everything, so it doesn't bother me at all that he's leaving. He has more than earned it, let him enjoy himself, let him rest," Cecilia Adriano, 52, told AFP.

Before the match, the University of Buenos Aires will award Messi an honorary doctorate.

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

No effort has been spared for the sendoff of a player considered one of the game's greatest ever.

Several of the teammates with whom he won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, and who will form the backbone of the post-Messi team, will play in the game, including defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.

After the game the captain's armband will pass to Romero.

Coach Lionel Scaloni has vowed to try to fill the "void" left by his talismanic captain and the signs from the next generation, some of whom weren't even alive when Messi debuted with the team in 2005, are promising.

In their first games since the World Cup final last week, minus Messi, Argentina thrashed Bolivia 4-0 in a friendly in Cordoba on Wednesday before running rings around Burkina Faso on Saturday at Monumental stadium.

Franco Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni, two of Argentina's brightest new hopes, both scored their first international goals in the 7-0 romp against Burkina Faso.

The results have begun the process of lifting the gloom of the defeat in the World Cup final when Argentina and a visibly tired Messi were outplayed by Spain in New Jersey.

Several of Messi's teammates resorted to thuggish tactics which were punished with bans and fines.

Messi is not only Argentina's most capped player but also its leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.

"La Pulga" (The Flea) won the eternal gratitude of Argentines -- and sealed his place as the rightful heir to Diego Maradona -- in 2022 when he ended their 36-year World Cup drought in Qatar.

During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina were also crowned 2005 world youth champions, 2008 Olympic champions and they won the Copa America in 2021 and 2024. They also won the 2022 Finalissima, a match between the champions of South America and Europe.

But there were tears along the way too, notably after Argentina's defeat by Germany in the 2014 World Cup final in Brazil, their 1-0 loss to Spain in this year's final and their shock defeat on penalties to Chile in the 2016 Copa America final.

One detail remains unclear, however: who will inherit Messi's coveted number 10 jersey?

"Until Leo's game, we won't give the number 10 to anyone," said Scaloni. "After that, we'll see."

articles.title: Man City charges: UEFA monitoring Premier League club's case as it considers potential action
articles.summary: Man City have denied any wrongdoing, claiming that they have a body of irrefutable evidence and have submitted their appeal; five of the charges the independent commission found City guilty of related to failing to comply with UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules
articles.body:
City have been found guilty by an independent commission of breaking the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, including five charges of failing to comply with UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules.

UEFA financial rules at the time meant clubs were effectively limited to spending what they earned within set break-even requirements.

The independent commission found that City's owners put in £830m of their own money and disguised it as sponsorship income for nine seasons.

City are appealing the decision and maintain they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence which will clear their name.

In 2014 City entered into a settlement agreement with UEFA which included a £49m (£32m of which was suspended) fine after they were charged with breaking Financial Fair Play rules.

In 2020 City were found guilty of breaking UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules, fined €30m (£25.4m) and banned from playing in European competitions for two years.

City appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sports and the ban was overturned, with CAS ruling that UEFA had not established that City's owners had disguised equity funding as sponsorship contributions, while other breaches were time-barred.

CAS reduced City's fine from €30m (£25.4m) to €10m (£8.5m) for failing to co-operate with the UEFA investigation and stated that most of the alleged breaches "were either not established or time barred".

UEFA has a statute of limitations of five years for financial rule breaches, whereas the Premier League does not have a statute of limitations.

UEFA's case was triggered by hacked City emails which were published by German magazine Der Spiegel in 2018.

City said the internal documents were "out-of-context materials purportedly hacked or stolen" as part of an "organised and clear attempt to damage the club's reputation".

The Premier League investigation had access to documents and evidence which were not available to UEFA when it were building its case against City.

City and UEFA have been contacted for comment.

Analysis: How long will Man City's appeal take?

"The appeal went in on Thursday at 7pm and so, according to the Premier League's rules, the appeal has to be done and dusted in 12 weeks from then, which takes us into the week before Christmas.

"The appeal can only last five days and those five days can only be in one block.

"The appeal panel, which has to be a different three-person panel from the original panel, would have 30 days to make up their minds and deliver their judgement. That would take you into the third week of January.

"Now that is the speeded-up timeline which has been introduced into the Premier League's rules this season.

"Now, Man City could argue that this speeded-up timeline should not apply in this case because this case has been going on for years and this new rule has only been introduced this season. That is something to look out for."

Details of Man City's appeal strategy explained

Latest from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas:

Manchester City are likely to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, Sky Sports News understands.

City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the independent commission, which "concluded it was an explanation that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".

However, it is understood City are expected to continue contesting this argument.

Manchester City is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Newton Investment and Development LLC. Sheikh Mansour is also a member of the ruling family of Abu Dhabi and he is the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The separation of UAE state investment and those that are private from the Abu Dhabi royal family has long been a subject of debate and criticism.

What did the independent commission find?

Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.

Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.

Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven.

The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.

Following the publication of the guilty verdict on September 29, a Manchester City statement read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

Why Man City's appeal could drag into 2027

Latest from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol and Amar Mehta:

Manchester City's appeal could drag on into next year if they argue that the process should not be run according to Premier League rules which were introduced for this season.

City have filed their appeal and the new rules about appeals state that this part of the disciplinary process has to be concluded within 12 weeks and the appeal hearing can last no longer than five days.

City's lawyers could argue that they were charged in 2023 and a hearing was held in 2024 - when the rules about a speeded-up appeals process were not in the Premier League Handbook.

A legal expert told Sky Sports News Manchester City would have a strong case for arguing that the new rules should not apply in this case.

The new rules were introduced to ensure that clubs, where possible, were punished in the same season as relevant rule breaches.
